Turning it off removes the permissions.
2. **Nothing leaves the browser unless the page IS a posting.** A local pre-check on the page (`JobPosting` JSON-LD, or a known ATS posting URL shape from the family table). A non-posting page sends **nothing** — not the URL, not a hash.
3. **Relevance is decided on the server, against the user's board** — the same D41 gates the board uses (US admission, the active profile's role family, fit) — and **an irrelevant posting is discarded server-side and never stored.** The relevant one goes through the ONE capture gateway (A62/D33) exactly as a manual capture does: dedup, US gate, enrichment, no second path.
4. **Migrated means on the board, silently, with a mark** — *Captured automatically* — and the popup lists *Captured today: N* with an undo per item (D53's bin).
5. **"Apply now" delivers the payload on that page.** If the tab is the application form (or becomes it), the packet is prepared right then (D56's *Prepare*) and the badge offers **Fill** — ⛔ **the fill still takes the user's click** and **Submit is never pressed** (D36). Auto-capture is not auto-apply.
6. **Rate-braked** — one capture per URL per user per day; a cap per hour; a kill switch beside `fullAutoDisabled()`.
7. **Manual capture stays as the fallback** until D64 has been seen working on real attended pages (O73); then the *Capture* button is demoted, not deleted.

⛔ **Compliance before the store:** a privacy-page section (what is read, when, that non-postings send nothing, the off switch), a `PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION` row, a `MANIFEST_RATIONALE` entry for the optional host permissions, and the Web Store *single purpose* text rewritten fresh (with F 4). LinkedIn / Indeed pages: **only if** the posting-detection and the server's refetch rules allow it — a page the server cannot refetch is captured from the user's own view, never by draft fetching it with the user's session.

### D65 · ⭐ WORK HISTORY AND SKILLS COME FROM THE RÉSUMÉ IN THE PAYLOAD

✅ **BUILT 10-07 (38c), local** — `1d216c7` (+ the active-profile widening in `217926d`). `services/payloadResume.js`: the résumé the packet CARRIES (its `resumes` artifact, else the active profile's base résumé, else the account's) parsed by the renderer's own `buildStructuredResume`; the parse stored WITH that résumé (**migration 138**, `parsed_json`/`parsed_basis` on `resumes`, `profile_base_resumes`, `base_resume`), re-parsed only when its text changes. A payload résumé is the ONE source of work history and its skills — no profile fallback beside it; a parse that reads nothing fills nothing there and says so; claimed skills (`confirmed_skills`) added, deduplicated, listed in `skillsClaimed`, filled even when the parse fails. `attachPacketResume` re-reads the entries when it attaches a résumé after the packet was built. All four of the row's tests, red when the fix is removed. ⚠ *"Have you worked here?"* (D55 f) still reads the base résumé when the packet's autofill payload is built before its résumé is known.

Owner 10-07: *"work history and skills would come from the parsed résumé currently being used to apply, the one in the payload. If that needs a migration that's what we'll do. The user might claim some skills and these should be filled in."*

- **Source of truth for the fill:** the résumé the packet carries (tailored, or the base under D66) is **parsed** into work history (employer, title, dates, location, bullets), education and skills, and that parse is what the extension fills into *Add Another* sections and skills fields. ⛔ Not the profile's stale copy, not a model call (D17 — parsing is in-house).
- **Store the parse with the artifact** — a migration if needed (e.g. `resume_parsed_json` on the generated résumé / base résumé row, written once when the résumé is written, re-parsed when it changes). The packet references it; it does not copy it.
- **User-claimed skills:** a profile list of skills the user claims that the résumé may not show; they are **added** to the fill's skills (deduplicated, never removed by the parse), marked as the user's own claim.
- *"Have you worked here before?"* (D55 f) reads the same parse — the company is in the payload résumé's work history → *Yes*; otherwise leave it for the user (never guess).
- ⛔ **Tests:** the fill's work-history entries equal the payload résumé's parse · a tailored résumé that dropped a role does not resurrect it · a claimed skill appears in the fill · a parse failure fills nothing for those sections and says so.

Owner's question, answered 10-07; decision pending.**~~ *Advantages of keeping it:* the exact confirmation page is the evidence (some portals identify the application only in the query — `?jobId=`, `gh_jid=`, `applicationId=`); it tells two applications on one portal apart; it can link straight back to the portal's status page. *Implications:* query strings also carry **session and one-time tokens, tracking ids (`utm_*`, `gclid`) and sometimes the applicant's email** — keeping them stores credentials-like secrets indefinitely as "evidence", widens what a breach exposes, and must be disclosed. **Recommendation: keep an allow-list of id-like parameters (`jobId`, `gh_jid`, `lever-*` ids, `applicationId`, `req`), drop everything else** — the evidence value without the tokens.

## ⛔ D76 · RAILWAY WEBHOOKS — deploy visibility and a volume alert — 2026-10-09

✅ Owner 10-09, after Railway's changelog (*custom headers for project webhooks*). **Why:** **Resume Master's `merge: A82 + A83 + …` deployment shows FAILED in the dashboard and nobody was told**; **O65** (*a push is not a deploy*) was found by accident; and **draft's volume reached 481 / 500 MB once.** Railway project webhooks push **deployment status changes and alert events** (a deployment failed or crashed, an out-of-memory kill, a volume alert, a monitor trigger) to **any URL**, configured **per project across all environments** — so one webhook covers `draft` **and** `resume-master`.

◐ **SET UP 10-07 (38g, late), on the owner's go:** `RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` generated locally (36 random bytes, kept in `draft-secrets/RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN.txt` under the owner's home folder, outside the repo; set on draft through the CLI's stdin; never printed) · **the project webhook created** (`ec579f62`) → `https://jobsviadraft.com/api/hooks/railway`, events failed · crashed · oom_killed · deployed · removed · VolumeAlert triggered / resolved · Monitor triggered / resolved, production only. ⛔ **Its `Authorization` header is NOT set:** the Railway tool takes no headers and the API refused the CLI's token for `notificationRuleUpdate` ("Not Authorized") — **the owner adds it in the dashboard** (Project Settings → Webhooks → the hook → Custom headers → `Authorization` = `Bearer ` + the file's contents); until then deliveries get 401 (harmless). ⭐ **Found while setting it up:** Railway's event NAMES (`deployed`, `redeployed`, `oom_killed`, `restarted`, `resumed`, `slept`) are not deployment statuses and the parser dropped them — fixed; `oom_killed` is an alarm. Was: ✅ **STEP 2 BUILT 10-07 (38g) ahead of Step 1, local, NOT pushed — migration 143.** Built first because the two unknowns were answerable from Railway's own docs (read through the Railway docs tool, `observability/webhooks`): ✅ **custom headers are real** (up to 20 per webhook, values write-only, sent with every delivery and with *Test Webhook*), and ⛔ **payloads are NOT signed** — the header IS the authentication. The payload is `{ type: "Deployment.<state>", details: { id, commitHash, commitAuthor, commitMessage, … }, resource: { workspace, project, environment, service, deployment }, severity, timestamp }`; delivery retries 3× and counts any 2xx/3xx as success. ⚠ **The volume- and monitor-alert type strings are NOT published** — accepted by family prefix (`Volume…`, `Monitor…`, `Alert…`); any other type is dropped with its NAME logged, so **the owner's *Test Webhook* reveals what Railway actually sends**.
- `POST /api/hooks/railway` (`routes/railwayHook.js`, mounted before the global parser): **`Authorization: Bearer <RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN>`**, constant-time; anything else **401 with no body** (no token on the server = the same 401: off, not open) · its own **16 KB** cap (413) · **60 / minute** per address (429) · `shared/deployEvents.js` keeps **the type, family, state, severity, project / environment / service names, service + deployment ids and the commit hash — never the commit message or author** (a person), malformed ids dropped · ⛔ read-only: one INSERT into `deploy_events`, an empty **204** whether kept or dropped, nothing echoed.
- **Admin → Ops → "Deployments"**: the last event per service — **red** for `failed` / `crashed` and for any volume / monitor alert (one rule, `isAlarm`) — with **this server's commit and latest applied migration** beside it, so a push that did not deploy shows.
- **Tests** `test/d76RailwayHook.test.js` (7): no / wrong header → 401, no body · unknown types dropped, same empty 204 · oversize 413, non-JSON 400 · **no table but `deploy_events` changes** · ids only · the rate limit · `Deployment.failed` → red, read through the shared rule — ⭐ four mutations (auth, the type rule, the cap, the alarm rule), each red. `npm test` **3813 / 3813 / 0**.
- **For the owner's Step 1, add to the webhook:** URL `https://jobsviadraft.com/api/hooks/railway` · a custom header `Authorization` = `Bearer <a long random value>` · the same value as `RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` on the draft service (batch it with the other pending variable changes — each restarts production) · press **Test Webhook** and read Admin → Ops (or the log line naming a dropped type). A second webhook to Discord / Slack for the human alert is unaffected.

**STEP 1 · THE OWNER — five minutes, no code:**
- A **Discord or Slack webhook** (Railway has built-in support for both) subscribed to **`Deployment.failed`**, **crashed**, **OOM killed**.
- A **volume alert on `draft-data` at ~80%** (and `resume-master-data`). ⚠ *Confirm the exact event names in the Webhooks tab — they are chosen from a list there.*
- **Check the service's `Backups` tab:** are **Railway's volume backups enabled for `draft-data`**, on what schedule, and has **one ever been restored into a scratch volume?** Draft's own daily backups live **on the same volume** as the database.

**STEP 2 · THE AGENT — small, after Step 1:** `POST /api/hooks/railway` — **a public endpoint, so it is hostile-input code:**
- ⛔ **Authenticate with a custom header** (`Authorization: Bearer …`, secret `RAILWAY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`), **constant-time compare**, refuse everything else with 401 and **no body.** ⚠ Confirm in the Webhooks tab that the header can be set — the owner reports the feature as shipped.

- **Draft's side:** `crawler_tasks`, `crawler_denylist` (seeded with the owner's five; **owner-editable**; a denial also refuses anything already queued), `services/crawlerQueue.js` (deny + SSRF at **queue** time, deny again at **lease** time, `CRAWLER_PAUSED`, a daily lease cap `CRAWLER_DAILY_TASKS` = 25), `routes/crawler.js` — worker doors **before** the JSON parser (the HMAC is over the exact bytes): `GET /api/crawler/next` · `/status` · `POST /result` (unsigned / mis-signed / stale → 401; a result accepted once); **no `CRAWLER_TOKEN` on draft = 503, off not open**; admin `GET/POST /api/admin/crawler`, `/tasks`, `/deny`. **J1 evidence → `harvestPairOf` (one parser, now also reading a BOARD's root and its API URLs) → the slug-harvest POOL** for the owner's review — nothing is added or enabled; unsupported vendors tallied (*icims*…). **J2 → an OBSERVED `apply_origin_pairs` row** (`crawler_seen_at`), **never promoted by the crawler** — `POST /api/admin/apply-origins/:id/promote` is the owner's, logged; **a shared host is refused** (A95; the Workday exception). **THE SHAPE IN FIVE LINES:**
1. ⛔ **A VM adds nothing to crawling postings** — the ATS boards are public JSON and the existing adapters stay in charge. **The pilot's two jobs:** **J1 find a company's board** (which ATS and slug — *the volume problem, D74 P3*) and **J2 learn where Apply lands** (D67 part 1, the sweep O84 says needs attended work). **J3 (custom career sites) is out of the pilot.**
2. ⛔ **A worker that cannot reach the database:** it **leases a task** from `GET /api/crawler/next` and **returns a signed result** to `POST /api/crawler/result`. **No DB credentials, no user data, no model call.** Its only secret is `CRAWLER_TOKEN`. **A separate service from the one that will hold user sessions (E3)** — the pilot rehearses that boundary.
3. **Ladder, browser last:** plain HTTP over `/careers` first (`detectKnownAtsMatch` already exists) → **only if empty and client-rendered**, the browser, reading **the network log** (the page's own call to `boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<slug>` is the best evidence). **Results go through the existing harvest → `validateBoard` → admin dry-run add. ⛔ Never auto-enabled.**
4. ⛔ **Rules of engagement — the line is ToS and robots, not technique:** **public pages only** · **`robots.txt` honoured** · an **identifying User-Agent** and a public `/crawler` page · **per-host rate limits** · **a fresh context per company** · **never** log in, type, submit, solve a CAPTCHA, evade a challenge or record a query string · **a data-driven, owner-editable DENY-LIST** (`linkedin.com`, `indeed.com`, `glassdoor.com`, `ziprecruiter.com`, `monster.com` …) that wins over every task · a takedown adds a domain the same day.
5. ⛔ **SSRF guard:** task URLs come from untrusted data — refuse `localhost`, private ranges, link-local and the cloud-metadata address, **re-checked after every redirect.**

**BUILD ORDER — so it is working shortly:**

✅ Owner 10-11 (setting up the Resend webhook): *"what else can the event listeners do?"* **What exists:** `routes/email.js` → `POST /api/hooks/resend` (Svix-signed over the RAW body, `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; **503 until the secret is set**), and `services/emailSuppression.js` → `recordEmailEvent`, which acts on **only two events**: `email.bounced` (a *Permanent* bounce) and `email.complained` → `email_suppressions`. **Every other event is accepted and ignored.** **Today the owner subscribes to those two only.**

**WHAT THIS ROW ADDS (small):** three more events, and one admin panel, so a broken sending path is **visible**:
- **`email.failed`** — a send errored (bad key, unverified domain, quota). **Raises an ADMIN alert** (Admin → Today) when it fires, and a louder one on **≥ 3 in an hour** — *a silent failure here means password resets stop arriving.*
- **`domain.updated`** — the domain's settings or verification changed (a DNS record lapsed). **Records the domain's status and alerts when it stops being verified.**
- **`email.suppressed`** — Resend itself blocked a send; **mirror the address into `email_suppressions`** (reason `provider_suppressed`) so draft stops trying too.
- *(optional, owner's word)* `email.delivery_delayed` — log only.
- ⛔ **NEVER subscribe to `email.opened` / `email.clicked`** (tracking — the policy says there is none), **`email.received`** (Cloudflare handles inbound) or **`contact.*`** (consent lives in draft's own database).

**THE PANEL — Admin → System → Email health (D83's six rules):** a one-sentence purpose · **numbers on open** — *the webhook secret is set (yes / no) · the last event received (when, what) · failed sends, last 7 days · suppressed addresses (total, new this week) · the domain's verification status* · **one main action: "Send a test to `bounced@resend.dev`"** (Resend's own safe test address) with a second for `complained@resend.dev` — *it proves the whole loop (Resend → the signed hook → the list) and says what it did* · **the suppression list**, searchable, with **Remove** for an address (a typed reason, an audit row, an undo — never silent) · both themes (D91), no pills (D60).

**HOW:** an **additive migration** (both runners, byte-identical): `email_events(svix_id PRIMARY KEY, type, received_at, email_id, detail)` — **`svix_id` makes a retried delivery idempotent** — and a `domain_status` row. ⛔ **Minimal personal data:** `email.failed` stores the **type, time, `email_id` and the provider's reason — NOT the recipient address**; the suppression list already holds addresses it must. **A retention sweep deletes `email_events` after 90 days.** The 64 KB body limit stays; an unknown event type returns **200** and is **ignored**; a bad signature returns **401**; the **`domain.updated` payload shape is read from Resend's docs in P0, not assumed.**

**PHASES:** **P0** read Resend's payloads for `email.failed`, `email.suppressed` and `domain.updated` and report them → **P1** the handler, the migration, the alert hook → **P2** the panel (built to the shared admin pattern; screenshots in both themes) → **P3** the owner adds the three events in Resend's dashboard.

**TESTS (each red when removed):** a **bad or missing signature is refused** · **a retried delivery (same `svix_id`) is recorded once** · `email.failed` raises an alert and stores **no recipient** · 3 failures in an hour raise the louder alert · `domain.updated` to *not verified* raises an alert and to *verified* clears it · `email.suppressed` adds the address · an unknown type returns 200 and changes nothing · a *temporary* bounce still does **not** suppress · Remove needs a reason and writes an audit row · the 90-day sweep deletes old events · admin-only; no model call; no opened / clicked handler exists.

**OWNER (after P2):** in Resend → Webhooks, **add `email.failed`, `email.suppressed` and `domain.updated`** to the existing webhook — *not before the handler exists.*

**THE FIVE RULES (a house rule from now on):** **(1) at most TWO visible surface levels per component** — a container and its controls, never a box in a box in a box · **(2) never clip a shadow** — a scroll or clip container gives shadows room, or clips with `clip-path: inset(-Npx 0)` · **(3) full-bleed decoration lives at PAGE level**, never inside a max-width column · **(4) sticky chrome blends in** — column width, feathered, never a hard full-width band · **(5) wells are for INPUTS only** — navigation controls are ghost until active.

**WHAT CHANGES / WHAT DOES NOT:** **colour tokens only.** **Neutrals (canvas, surfaces, text, borders) go to PURE black and white — no cream, no warm charcoal; the BRAND STAYS: the logo orange, and green / red / amber / blue for indicators and fit bands — each re-tuned to the theme's contrast target.** **Depth, glass, grain, radii, type, spacing, layout, copy are UNTOUCHED** (effects are a separate axis from colour). ⛔ **DOCUMENTS ARE NEVER THEMED** — the résumé preview, the PDF / DOCX and the cover letter stay black on white in every theme; company logos stay on their paper tile. **Targets:** text **7:1 (AAA)** · control edges, focus rings, chart segments **4.5:1** · the label on the orange fill **4.5:1** (⚠ black on `#FD4600` is **6.05:1** — better than today's 5.02:1, AA not AAA; reaching 7:1 needs a lighter fill ≈ `#FF6A1F`; **owner decides**, default keep the brand).

**THE MODULE — a theme is DATA, one file:** `client/src/themes/{index,paper-light,charcoal-dark,contrast-light,contrast-dark}.js` — `{ id, label, scheme, contrast:'aa'|'aaa', tokens, substrate }`; **`index.js` is the ONLY place a theme is chosen.** **Adding a theme = one new file + one registry line, no component changes** (`docs/THEMES.md`: five steps). **Contract, each a test:** every theme supplies **every** key · every declared pair passes at the theme's own target · **a contrast theme's neutrals are R = G = B and its chromatics are only the brand set** (orange, green, red, amber, blue, violet, teal) · light and dark neutrals invert · hex is 6-digit · **the colour-literal count reaches ZERO.** **Remaining tokens are DERIVED, not copied:** `scripts/deriveThemeTokens.mjs` keeps each hue and moves only lightness, in the smallest step that meets the target on every pair the token is declared in; a person reviews. Third-party sign-in buttons keep their brand colours.

**SHAPE CUES — a USER SETTING, not a theme (default OFF):** `data-cues="shape"` adds a **glyph + edge style** to status marks (✓ solid · ! dashed · ✕ double · i dotted), a **fill style** to fit bands (filled · hatched · outlined · dashed) and **patterns** to chart segments — for ANY theme, **implemented ONCE in the shared mark / band / segment components**; the audit lists every place that bypasses them. *(Orange and amber are close — this is the mitigation.)*

**HOW A PERSON GETS IT:** **Settings → Appearance** (four preview cards + the Shape-cues switch) · **saved to the ACCOUNT** (an additive `appearance` setting; the mobile contract bumps additively) and cached locally, **no flash on load** · `prefers-color-scheme` picks light or dark · **`prefers-contrast: more` OFFERS the Contrast pair, never forces it** · **`prefers-reduced-transparency` → opaque glass** · **`forced-colors` is honoured — every control has a real border** · the extension builds from the same registry. ⛔ **No new permission, no new data leaves the page.**

**SCOPE:** marketing, auth, the board, Draft House, The Table, the posting panel and ATS report, Settings, Help, **every Admin panel**, menus / modals / toasts / tooltips, the extension's popup / options / badge / review overlay. **Out:** Resume Master's site, the Android app, emails, documents.

**PHASES — each reported before the next:** **P0 AUDIT (read-only, `docs/THEME_AUDIT.md`: every literal by area, every inline `theme.*` / `isDark` branch, every place that draws its own status / band / chart colour, every place meaning rides on hue alone, what `C_DARK` is used for and whether dark is reachable, the extension pipeline, a size estimate per area) → P1 THE MODULE with ZERO visual change (⛔ Paper Light pixel-identical on every screenshot; all existing tests pass) → P2 burn the literals to zero area by area, each batch pixel-diffed → P3 the contrast token sets + the derivation script + the contrast proof → P4 shape cues → P5 Settings → Appearance + persistence + system preferences → P6 COVERAGE: the screenshot matrix — every route × four themes × desktop and phone × cues off and on — no page error, no contrast failure, focus visible everywhere → P7 `docs/THEMES.md`.** ⛔ **Nothing ships before the owner reviews P6's matrix.**

**TESTS (each red when removed):** key parity · pairs at target · neutrals R=G=B and brand-only chromatics · light / dark neutrals invert · literals = 0 · **Paper Light unchanged (P1)** · **documents render black on white in every theme** · shape cues cause no reflow and add a glyph and edge style to every mark · a theme chosen on one device appears on the next · no flash · forced-colors shows a border on every control · reduced transparency makes glass opaque · **the extension's generated tokens equal the registry's** · no new request, storage key or permission.

**OWNER DECIDES (defaults; the agent starts P0 regardless):** names (*Contrast Light / Contrast Dark*) · the brand fill (*keep `#FD4600`*) · the mark in Contrast Dark (*all-orange*) · grain (*keep, neutral*) · amber and blue (*kept*) · offer the pair under `prefers-contrast: more` (*offer, never force*).

**THE SHAPE:** **one list, one detail page made of modules.** **Admin → Users** (the list) → **a user's page = a stack of reusable PANEL MODULES.** **The same modules render read-only or limited in the user's OWN Settings** (tickets, usage, connected apps, sessions) — *one set of components, two audiences.* **A module contract:** `{ id, title, audience: ['admin','self'], loader(userId), actions[], render }` in a registry — **adding a module is one registry entry.** **Shared parts:** the panel shell (purpose sentence · number boxes · one primary action · history with Undo), `ConfirmWrite` (states exactly what changes and for how many), `EntitlementRow`, `HistoryList`.

**THE MODULES (v1):**
1. **Account & status** — who, created, last active, email verified, plan, **status (active · suspended · pending deletion)**, tags (*internal · test · beta*), a private note. ⛔ **Eligibility answers (sponsorship, work authorisation, clearance, EEO) are NEVER shown here** — sensitive and irrelevant to support.
2. **Tickets** — *the first module built.* **User side:** Settings → Help → *Contact support* (category · subject · message; **context attached automatically** — account id, app version, page; **no attachments in v1**, they carry personal data). **Admin side:** a queue (open · waiting on user · solved), assign, priority, **internal notes the user never sees**, canned replies, a **due date** (SLA), **category `privacy_request` with a legal deadline timer** (*30 days GDPR, 45 CCPA — owner confirms*) and a link to the account's export and delete tools. **Replies go by Resend from `support@jobsviadraft.com` with Reply-To `support@`**; the thread lives in-app. *Phase 2: inbound mail to `support@` becomes a ticket via a Cloudflare Worker that POSTs to draft.* ⛔ No model replies (D17).
3. **Plan & usage** — **the plan** (free · beta · pro · custom; **a record, so billing (Stripe) can attach later — payments are NOT in this row**) with since / expiry; **usage meters with reset times** — draft slots used, résumés today / this month, previews, submitted applications, plugin calls; a **grant** (*+10 drafts for 7 days, with a reason*); **admin-only: our internal cost for this user** (the ledger; users never see money — see the cost-hiding prompt).
4. **Feature access** — **the registry of entitlements, one row each: *effective value · where it comes from · override · reason · expiry · who set it.*** **Features:** `plugin_byo` (the D86 bring-your-own-model plugin, boolean) · `byo_daily_cap` · `draft_slots` per day · `resume_generations_per_day` · `a_plus_enabled` · `auto_apply_mode` (*locked · attended*) · beta flags. ⛔ **ONE RESOLVER: `entitlements.resolve(user, feature)` — order: the GLOBAL kill switch → the user's override → the plan default → the system default** — *the UI shows the winning source ("plan: beta", "override by owner, expires 12 Oct").* ⛔ **Hard ceilings are not overridable**: **full auto stays LOCKED whatever a row says (D36)**, and a per-user value cannot exceed a system maximum. **Enforced SERVER-SIDE at every use** (generate, plugin tools, drafting) — *a hidden button is not a control.* The user's own plugin switch (D86) and the admin's per-user permission are **both** required.
5. **Connected apps & sessions** *(shares D86 and the sessions task)* — apps connected, **Revoke**; active sessions, **Sign out everywhere**.
6. **Activity & audit** — one timeline: logins, generations, applications, tickets, **and every admin change**, each from `admin_audit_log` (D58) — *actor · action · before → after · reason.* ⛔ **Immutable.**

**ADMIN → USERS (the list):** server-paginated table — *user · plan · status · last active · email verified · drafts used / limit · résumés this week · applications · open tickets · an **override-active** mark.* **Search** (email, id, name) · **filters** (plan, status, open ticket, has override, inactive N days, created range, **hide internal and test accounts**) · sort · **saved views** · **number boxes on top** (total · active this week · suspended · open tickets · near their cap). **Row → the user's page.**
**UTILITIES (each one confirmed, audited, reversible where it can be):** **resend the verification email** · **send a password-reset link** (*never set a password*) · **sign out everywhere** · **revoke connected apps** · **suspend / unsuspend** with a reason · **grant allowance** · **change plan** · **set or clear an override** · **export the user's data** (JSON, the user's own data only) · **delete the account: soft, a grace period, then hard — irreversible, a typed confirmation** · **add a note or tag** · **bulk actions with a dry run and a recipient ceiling** (grant, change plan, send a notice via D73's notice tool, export a CSV). ⛔ **NO impersonation in v1** — *the owner decides; if wanted later: time-limited, ticket-linked, read-only, fully audited.* **A read-only "see what this user sees" view built from the same modules is the safe substitute.** **Roles:** `admin` (everything) and `support` (tickets, read, resend verification, notes — **no delete, plan or override changes**) — *so the dev can help without the keys.*

**DATA (both migration runners, byte-identical):** reuse what exists first — *report it in Phase 0.* New: `user_entitlement_overrides(user_id, feature_key, value_json, reason, set_by, set_at, expires_at, revoked_at)` · `user_plan(user_id, plan_key, since, expires_at, source)` · `tickets(id, user_id, category, subject, status, priority, assignee, source, created_at, updated_at, due_at)` · `ticket_messages(id, ticket_id, author_type, author_id, body, internal, created_at)` · `user_notes` · `user_tags` · `users.status` + `suspended_reason`. **Plans and feature defaults live in code** (`shared/entitlements.js`) — *versioned, tested, one source.*

**PRIVACY (moves with the code):** tickets hold personal data — **a retention period, deleted with the account, disclosed in the policy and `PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION`**; an admin **read of sensitive content is a logged "reveal" with a reason** (résumé bodies are hidden by default); the list shows only what the work needs.

**PHASES — each reported before the next:** **P0 · INVENTORY (read-only):** the users table, the existing caps and exactly where each is enforced (draft slots, Settings → Applying), what Admin → Users shows today, the usage ledger, `admin_audit_log`, any role or suspend notion, and **how it overlaps D83's `ADMIN_AUDIT.md`**. **P1 · THE RESOLVER** — move the existing caps behind it with **NO change in any default**; tests prove today's behaviour is identical. **P2 · THE SKETCH** (the owner approves) **then the shell + modules 1, 3, 4, 6.** **P3 · TICKETS** (user side, admin queue, Resend). **P4 · THE LIST + UTILITIES + roles.** **P5 · THE SELF-SERVICE SUBSET in Settings.** **P6 · LATER:** inbound email as tickets, billing, the impersonation decision.

⛔ **TESTS (each red when removed):** the resolver's order holds · **a per-user override cannot unlock full auto or exceed a ceiling** · **every capped feature is enforced on the server** (a direct API call over the cap is refused) · a `support` role **cannot** delete, change a plan or set an override · **every admin write writes an audit row** and the timeline shows it · a sensitive reveal needs a reason and is logged · **a ticket's internal note never reaches the user** · deleting an account removes or anonymises its tickets · a bulk action refuses past its ceiling and its dry run changes nothing · **no eligibility field appears in any module** · both themes; no capsule shapes (D60).

⛔ **NOT IN THIS ROW:** payments and subscriptions billing · teams / organisations · SSO · a chat widget · model-written replies · impersonation. **THE OWNER DECIDES:** **the plan tiers and their default limits** · **the ticket categories and response targets** · **the retention period and the deletion grace period** · **whether the `support` role exists yet** · **impersonation, yes or no.**

> **What was decided in the build:** (1) **the guard is VENDORED, not called** — `services/resumeClaimGuard.js` was already a copy of the tools service's `src/integrity` (identical but for one comment), so draft calls it directly; the new **term guard** sits beside it in `services/byom/resumePatch.js`. (3) **DCR, not CIMD** — CIMD (OpenAI's preferred) means fetching a URL the client names; it waits for its own SSRF review (A96). (4) **Only Claude's and ChatGPT's redirect hosts may register** — an arbitrary site cannot phish a consent. (5) **The operator's switch defaults OFF**, so the push turns nothing on — *who sees it first* stays the owner's. (6) **No Draft slot and no plan generation is spent**; the per-user cap is 50 saved résumés a day. (7) ⚠ **The privacy sentence was NARROWED** — the brief sends the job's title, company, level, location and matched keywords, not the posting text; the policy, the consent screen and Settings say exactly that.

✅ Owner 10-09: *"explore the plugins — can a user use their own ChatGPT account and subscription for the résumé generation part?" — "build this now."* **Verdict: feasible.** **The model that writes the résumé is the user's; draft supplies a brief and VALIDATES what comes back — so draft makes NO model call (D17 holds) and pays nothing for generation (D70's ~13¢ goes to zero for these résumés).** ⛔ **An OPTION beside today's generation, never a replacement.**

**THE FACTS (researched 10-09 — ⛔ PHASE 0 re-verifies each in OpenAI's own docs; several came from third-party guides):** the Apps SDK is **built on MCP** (launched 10-2025, directory open to submissions 12-2025) · **the App directory became the *Plugin* directory on 07-09-2026 — a plugin can hold skills, an MCP app and templates** · sign-in is **OAuth 2.1** (ChatGPT is the client: **dynamic client registration, PKCE, refresh tokens required**) · **plan access varies** (OpenAI's help says installing or using a specific plugin depends on plan, workspace, role and surface; *one guide: custom apps in developer mode — write actions on Business / Enterprise / Edu, read-only on Pro*) · *a guide's submission checklist:* **live privacy policy AND terms of service, domain verification, OAuth with OpenAI's redirect URI, annotated tools with a justification each, ≥ 5 positive test prompts, light and dark icons** · **Claude custom connectors work on the same MCP server** (D21).

**PHASE 0 · VERIFY (no build; report):** (a) **who pays for the model inside a plugin** — OpenAI's explicit statement; (b) **which plans can install and use a custom or directory plugin**, and **what developer mode allows** (⛔ *does the owner's own testing need a Business workspace?*); (c) **the review criteria and the policies on résumé / personal data**; (d) **Claude's connector availability by plan**; (e) **whether the host exposes MCP sampling** — *the design does NOT rely on it.* ⛔ **If (b) blocks the owner's own testing, say so before Phase 1.**

**PHASE 1 · THE TWO-TOOL CORE (⛔ hosted in DRAFT — accounts, jobs and the résumé store live there; Resume Master's MCP stays anonymous for public tools):**
1. **`get_generation_brief(job_id)` — read-only (`readOnlyHint`).** Returns **only** what the model needs: the candidate's **base résumé as structured bullets WITH IDS** · their **claims** · **the matched and claimed keywords and verbs (D70's keywords-only context — never the posting's unclaimed requirements)** · the job's title, company, level and location · **our instructions and the OUTPUT SCHEMA.** ⛔ **The brief carries NO contact details — no email, phone or address — the server writes the header itself.** ⛔ **A brief is single-use, bound to `(user, job, base-résumé hash)`, and expires (~30 min).**
2. **`submit_resume(brief_id, patch)` — a write (`readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`, idempotent per brief).** ⭐ **The model returns a PATCH — only the bullets it rewrites, keyed by id, plus the skills order and an optional summary — NOT a whole résumé** (D70 Phase 2: it cannot touch a date, an employer or a title, and it is cheaper in the user's tokens). **The server renders the résumé deterministically, runs THE CLAIM GUARD (no term that is in neither the base résumé nor the claims; titles, employers and dates unchanged), scores it with `scoreAtsLocally`, stores the artifact (D16 / D57, *résumé ready*, base → tailored per D58), and returns the score plus a link.** ⛔ **A guard refusal returns each reason in plain words so the model can revise and resubmit — at most 3 attempts per brief.** ⚠ *The guard lives in Resume Master (`src/integrity`); the agent decides whether draft calls it as a deterministic validate route (no model) or vendors it — and says which.*
3. **Supporting, read-only:** `score_resume(job_id, content)` · `list_my_drafts()` · `get_my_resumes()`. **Every tool has its annotations and a written justification** (the review requires both).

**THE AUTH — O16c, now concrete (⛔ the real build):** draft becomes **an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the plugin**: **authorization-code + PKCE (S256), dynamic client registration, refresh tokens, resource indicators, `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and authorization-server metadata**; a **consent screen** — *"Allow ChatGPT to read your profile and save résumés to draft?"* — with scopes **`resume:read`** and **`resume:write`**; **Settings → Connected apps** to see and **revoke** each connection; **token lifetimes; per-user rate limits** (*a separate daily cap for bring-your-own-model résumés, ~50, to stop abuse*); **an audit row per tool call.** ⛔ **The plugin never uses a browser cookie; a token never reaches the extension's credential store** (the extension keeps its own, auth.js). *Use the MCP SDK's auth helpers; a managed provider (a new vendor) is the alternative — the agent states the trade.*

**PRIVACY (⛔ moves with the code):** the policy and `PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION` get a row — *"If you use draft through ChatGPT or Claude, your résumé content and the job description are processed by that provider under YOUR account and its terms"* — and **the consent screen says the same.** ⛔ **A live terms-of-service page is required for submission — confirm one exists.**

**UI — WHERE THE SWITCHES GO (owner, 10-09: *"add UI-side switches for the plugin and sign-in to OpenAI — show me how and where"*; sketch `plugin-ui.html` — ⛔ build to the file, not this prose; the same text is in `D86_UI_ADDENDUM.md`).**

⛔ **THE DIRECTION OF SIGN-IN IS THE REVERSE OF WHAT WAS ASKED, AND THE UI SAYS SO.** **There is NO "Sign in with OpenAI" button in draft.** The user **adds draft's plugin INSIDE ChatGPT**; **ChatGPT sends them to draft's own consent screen** (OAuth 2.1). *draft cannot sign in to a user's OpenAI account to use their subscription.* **Phase 0 must confirm that OpenAI offers no "sign in with ChatGPT to use my plan" route for third-party apps** *(one exists for OpenAI's own tools; assume none for us).* So draft's UI **controls and shows** the connection and **meets the user where they are.**

**FIVE PLACEMENTS:**
1. **SETTINGS → CONNECTED APPS — the one persistent home.** A one-sentence purpose · **ONE master switch, OFF by default** — *"Write my résumés in ChatGPT or Claude"* — **nothing connects until it is on** · **number boxes:** résumés written this way today **(x / 50)**, apps connected · **ONE plain sentence on the screen:** *what an app can do* (read the base résumé and claims; save a résumé), *what it never sees* (contact details, passwords, applications, other jobs), *what leaves draft* (the résumé content and the job description, **under the user's own account and the provider's terms**) · **a plain card per host** (ChatGPT, Claude): **Not connected** → *"How to connect — you do this in ChatGPT, not here"*, three steps, **Open ChatGPT to connect**, **Copy the plugin link**, and *while in private testing* a **"private testing" notice that must vanish when the plugin is published**; **Connected** → last used, how many résumés, **Disconnect** (*stops its next call at once*) · **a Recent-activity list** — the per-call audit, in plain words, **no résumé content.**
2. **THE RÉSUMÉ BUTTON — the point of use.** In the posting panel's sticky action bar (D48 / D49) **the Résumé control becomes a SPLIT BUTTON** — one click is the default; the caret chooses: **Write it with draft** (*uses a draft credit*) · **Write it in ChatGPT** (*free to you — your own ChatGPT*) · **Write it in Claude** · *a link to Settings if the apps are off.* **A four-step status that updates ITSELF while the user is in the chat:** *Open ChatGPT → Waiting for your résumé… → Checks → Done.* **A guard refusal shows in plain words and says "Nothing was saved".** **The result: *Résumé ready · base 62 → 78 · claims checked*, with View and Download.** ⚠ *"Open ChatGPT" with the request pre-filled depends on ChatGPT accepting a prefilled prompt link — Phase 0 confirms; otherwise the button COPIES the request.* In the narrow (icon) layout the choice sits in a menu.
3. **INSIDE CHATGPT / CLAUDE — what the plugin looks like.** Tool calls as **labelled boxes with a read-only / write mark**; a guard refusal the model explains; **the result as a CARD** — score, base → tailored, **Open in draft**, **Download PDF**. ⛔ **The tool descriptions and the refusal text are written so ANY model explains them plainly.**
4. **THE CONSENT SCREEN — draft's own page, where "sign in" really happens** (draft's session; **no password goes to ChatGPT**): *"ChatGPT wants to connect to your draft account"* · **signed in as … · Not you?** · **explicit scopes** (read the base résumé and claims — *required*; save résumés) **and an on-screen *Never* list** · **the privacy sentence** · **Allow / Not now.** ⛔ **If the Connected-apps switch is OFF, the consent screen says so and offers to turn it on — it never fails silently.**
5. **ADMIN → SYSTEM → PLUGIN — the operator (D83's six rules).** A purpose sentence · **numbers:** users connected, résumés this week, **the share that passed the claim check first time**, refused-and-fixed · **a GLOBAL FEATURE SWITCH — the kill switch — that states what happens when it is off** · **a HOST ALLOW-LIST** (ChatGPT, Claude separately) · **a per-user daily cap setting** · **recent tool calls** (time, user, tool, result — **never content**).

⛔ **TESTS (each red when removed):** **the master switch is OFF by default and no connection works while it is off** · **the global switch refuses every tool call and the Settings card reads "unavailable"** · **a disabled host cannot connect** · **Disconnect stops the very next call** · **the consent screen shows the *Never* list and the privacy sentence** · **the résumé button's default is unchanged for a user who never enables the feature** · **no résumé content appears in the activity list or the admin log.**

**EVIDENCE** *(the owner's export `enrichment-export-20261008-1816.jsonl`, filled and applied, undo proven):* **17 of 20 exported descriptions had their MIDDLE CUT OUT** (the export caps text at 5,000 characters, keeps the head and the tail, and writes `[…]` between) — **and the stored pay for DoorDash (107,400–158,000) and Zscaler (185,500–265,000 and 133,000–190,000) is absent from the exported text.** · **`summary` was pre-filled on 20 of 20 rows as the first 300 characters of the posting verbatim** (*"ABOUT US…"*), `normalized_title` as the lowercased title, **`experience_level` by a title heuristic — 8 of 20 differ from the text (Staff / Principal stored as `senior`)**, `workplace_type` on 12 of 20 where the text is silent. · **Pay stated in the text and never captured: 10 of 13 postings** — incl. `Salary range: $110,000 - $140,000`. · Board coverage: **skills 14%** — **~2,850 postings still need enrichment.** · 3 of the 20 were **identical text posted in two locations.**

**P1 — BEFORE ANY BATCH OF 480:**
- **F1 · THE EXPORT MUST NOT CUT THE MIDDLE.** ⛔ Send the **cleaned full text** (`description_text`, D59) with **boilerplate removed first** — equal-opportunity, benefits and perks, *about us*, legal and privacy notices, recruitment-scam and AEDT notices — **and NEVER a paragraph about requirements, qualifications, responsibilities, tech stack, pay, location, workplace, visa, sponsorship, or clearance.** Raise the cap to **12,000 characters**; if a posting is still longer, **cut the boilerplate-classified tail, never the middle**, set **`truncated: true`** and report **`chars_sent` / `chars_total`** per row. ⛔ **`[…]` must never appear in an export.** *Measure first:* the distribution of description length across the board — the share over 5,000 / 8,000 / 12,000. ⛔ **A row enriched from truncated text is `partial` and re-enters the backlog** (the import records it). **Rows already enriched from cut text** (the 20 — and any later) **are identified by re-deriving their export text, marked `partial`, and re-run with the OVERWRITE switch on `skills_json` only — a batch, revertible.** *Tests: the DoorDash and Zscaler fixtures export their pay and requirements; no export contains `[…]`.*
- **F2 · CRAWLER PLACEHOLDERS ARE NOT ENRICHMENT.** Give each enrichment column a **provenance** (`crawler_fallback` · `import` · `owner`). **A `crawler_fallback` value counts as EMPTY** for *fill empty only* and may be replaced; **an `import` or `owner` value is never replaced without the OVERWRITE switch.** **Backfill the provenance by detection:** `summary` equal to the first 300 characters of the description; `normalized_title` equal to the lowercased title; `experience_level` and `workplace_type` set by the heuristic. ⛔ **One shared mapping for level** — *intern · entry (new grad, junior, associate, I, 0–2 yrs) · mid (II, 3–5 yrs) · senior (Senior, 6+) · lead (Staff, Principal, Lead, Manager, Director) · executive (VP, C-level)* — **used by the crawler fallback AND the model prompt**, so **Staff / Principal are no longer stored as `senior`.** `workplace_type` taken from the board's own `location: Remote` is **stated, with the source recorded.**
- **F5 · THE DRY RUN MUST SHOW PER-COLUMN COUNTS.** *"Would be written 20"* hid that **three columns write 0 and three write 10.** Add **a per-column table: already filled · supplied · WOULD BE WRITTEN** (and, per F2, *replacing a placeholder*).
- **F13 · A NOTES CHANNEL, SO SCRUTINY IS CAPTURED.** The prompt asks the model for **`#NOTE <job_id> <code> <≤ 20 words>` lines after the JSONL** — codes: `TRUNCATED` · `PAY-FORMAT` · `PLACEHOLDER` · `NOT-CS` · `NON-US` · `DUPLICATE` · `ODD`. **The upload check skips `#NOTE` lines, collects them, and shows them on the page under *"Things the model flagged"*, with a count by code and a CSV download** — *instead of today's "unreadable line".* Until it ships, the notes travel as **chat text beside the file**, not inside it.
- ⛔ **THE EXPORT HEADER:** strip the **`_meta`** line and **`stored_content_hash`** from every piece.

- **F14 · ONE BIG BATCH, ONE DOWNLOAD, ONE UPLOAD (owner, 10-09: *"it's broken into 17 pieces — I have to download 17 and upload 17. 30 a batch is too small. Do it all at once, or at least a batch download and upload."*).** ⛔ **The pieces exist only because one chat can read so much — NOT because the import needs them.** So: **(a) the batch is as big as the importer allows — raise the 500 cap to 2,000** (`≤ 32 MB`; *the import is all-or-nothing in one transaction — the agent confirms there is no real limit below that*); **(b) the piece size is a SETTING** — *20 · **50 (recommended)** · 100* — and **it governs only the chat step**; **(c) ONE "Download all pieces (.zip)"**; **(d) ONE "Upload all the replies" — choose or drop many files; the page matches each reply to its piece BY FILE NAME and checks them all together**; **(e) a compact grid of piece squares** (green = checked) **instead of one row each**; **(f) one Join, one dry run, one Apply and ONE Undo for the whole batch.** ⚠ **A name that matches no piece, or two replies for one piece, is reported, never guessed.** *Sketch: `admin-enrichment.html`.* ⛔ **The honest limit:** the chat step is still **one chat per piece** — **a 500-row batch at 50 per chat is 10 chats**, 2,000 at 100 is 20. *That is what F9 and the optional option below are for.*
- ⏸ **THE OWNER DECIDES — an optional owner-run script that fills EVERY piece through the Anthropic Batch API with the owner's own key, outside the product (never deployed, never imported by the server; D17 holds).** *Cost, rough:* ~3,300 postings ≈ 4M input and ~1.3M output tokens ≈ **about $2 on a Haiku-class model or about $11 on a Sonnet-class one at the Batch API's 50% discount — the figures are estimates to be re-checked against current pricing.* **It removes the chat loop entirely and returns one file.** *The owner objected to needing a key and a terminal — this is the trade: ~$10 and one command against about 66 chats for the whole backlog.* **Not built unless the owner asks.**

**P2 — SOON, AND CHEAPER THAN THE MODEL:**
- **F3 · THE PAY PARSER (D71) HAS TO RUN AT INGEST AND TOLERATE REAL FORMATS.** *Only 3 of 13 postings that state pay had it captured — and those 3 were not in the exported text at all (they came from the board's structured field).* **Run the prose parser on every new posting and backfill the board.** **Fixtures, verbatim from the 20:** `Annual salary range: $180,000- $240,000` · `Annual salary range:  $180,000-$240,000 USD` · `Salary range: $110,000 - $140,000` · ⛔ `Salary range: $190,000 $250,000 + performance-based bonus` *(NO separator)* · `Salary range: $180,000 $260,000 Base Salary + performance-based bonus` · ⛔ `$187,500 - 220,000 USD` *(the second figure has no `$`)* · `$187,500 - $220,000 USD base salary`. **Rules:** two figures count as a range **when a pay label precedes them** (*salary range, base salary, pay range, compensation*) **even without a dash**, or when **both** carry a currency symbol; a trailing `+ bonus / equity / USD` is ignored; **negatives:** `401k contributions and 4% match`, revenue and headcount.
- **F7 · DEDUPE IDENTICAL TEXT.** 3 of 20 rows were **the same text in two locations** (multi-location companies post one role many times). **Export one representative per distinct text hash with `applies_to: [job_ids]`; the import expands it to every row sharing that text** — *after verifying the texts really are identical.* Saves 15–30% of the effort on multi-location boards.
- **F8 · DON'T ENRICH WHAT THE BOARD WILL DROP.** **Exclude** rows that D78 will retire (out of scope, older than 120 days, non-US) from the backlog count and the export, and **order the export** *without a fit score first, then newest*.

**P3 — THE STRATEGIC ANSWER TO ~2,850 ROWS:**
- **F6 · CANONICAL SKILL NAMES.** The prompt requires **canonical forms** (*PostgreSQL* not *Postgres*; *Google Cloud Platform* not *GCP*; *Kubernetes* not *K8s*); **the merge maps aliases to the D72 vocabulary and sends unknown terms to its review queue.**
- ⭐ **F9 · USE THE ENRICHED BATCHES AS A LABELLED SET.** A model fills skills at a few minutes a piece; **a deterministic phrase-match extractor** (the D72 vocabulary, no model) **fills them in milliseconds.** **After ~2 batches, measure the extractor's precision and recall against the model's skills on the same postings — and where it clears the bar, run it over the rest of the board and use the model only for a sample and the exceptions.** *(The agent's earlier note — "automatic extraction at ingest wouldn't help" — should be re-examined against this: **the reason is wanted in the report.**)*

**INTERIM — SO THE OWNER CAN START NOW WITHOUT WASTE:** add an export filter **"complete text only"** (no cut: ~15% of postings, ~430 rows) — **batch 1 runs on those**, and F1's rows follow. ⛔ **Do not enrich the cut ones until F1 ships.**

**THE BATCH PROCESS** *(480 = 24 pieces of 20 — the piece size becomes a setting; **default 20 with full text**, because 30 full postings is ~100k tokens)*: **a fresh chat per piece**, the **prompt v2** (`ENRICHMENT_PROMPT_V2.txt`) pasted first, the piece attached, **the reply saved as a file, and the model's NOTES copied beside it.** The notes of each batch are pasted into the findings thread and **become the next fixes**; the **known-issues list** travels in the prompt so a fresh chat does not rediscover them.

⛔ **Tests (each red when removed):** no export contains `[…]` or `_meta` · a row with pay in the cut middle exports its pay · a `crawler_fallback` summary is replaced on import and an `import` value is not · Staff / Principal map to `lead` in the crawler and the prompt · the dry run lists per-column counts · a `#NOTE` line is collected and not rejected · each pay fixture above parses and each negative does not · identical text exports once and imports to every row.

**WHAT THE SCREENSHOT SHOWED:** an *Enrichment backlog* panel with a number field (*"up to 100"*), a free-text *source* box and one loud button, **Count the backlog**, that shows no result on screen — and a paragraph saying the real work is on **another page** (Database → Enrichment Round Trip); directly beneath, a *Job data — in and out* panel. **Three "data in and out" places, and nothing says how they differ.** The label carries *"(D17)"* — a design-doc code. **Undo is an API route in the agent's notes.**

**THE SIX RULES — every admin panel is judged against them:**
1. **One sentence of purpose**, in plain words; **project codes live behind a `?` tooltip.**
2. **The state as NUMBERS, with no click** — big figures first (how many, how full, how old).
3. **One obvious next step** — one accent button; **a harmless read is never the loudest control.**
4. **A path where there is a process** — numbered steps; **a step unlocks only when the one before is done, and says why it waits.**
5. **Every write has a marker and an undo** — a confirm stating **exactly what changes and how many rows**; **a history with Undo beside each entry.**
6. **Plain words, real controls** — **dropdowns of real values, never a free-text box for a known set**; no capsules (D60); both themes; keyboard-operable.
*Rule 4 only fits a process; a plain table (Users) needs rules 1, 2, 3 and 6.*

**BUILD 1 — THE ENRICHMENT PAGE (the pilot for the pattern).** **One page, six steps:** *(1) Count — automatic, shown as done · (2) Export a batch — rows (≤ 500, the importer's own cap) and a **source dropdown of the real sources** · (3) Fill it outside the product — **the two `enrichmentChunks.mjs` commands on screen with Copy buttons**, and `PROMPT.txt` named · (4) Dry run — the result table (matched · would write · unchanged · refused, **each refusal reason counted**) and **the projected coverage before → after** · (5) Apply — **locked until a clean dry run of that exact file**; a confirm *"This writes 492 postings. All or nothing. You can undo it."* · (6) Check or undo.* **Above the steps: four number boxes** (postings needing enrichment · share of new postings with a fit score · imports so far · batches left to clear it) and **per-column coverage bars** (skills · level · workplace · salary · eligibility flags · summary). **Below: *Past imports* with an Undo on every batch** (the revert route behind a button). ⛔ **The allowed values, the 500 cap and the coverage figures are READ from the importer and the live board — never a copy that can drift.** ⛔ The two safety switches (*fill empty columns only*, *refuse changed postings*) **stay on and are shown as on**; turning one off is an explicit, labelled expert action.

**BUILD 1b — STEPS 2–4 MUST BE SELF-EXPLANATORY (owner, 10-09: *"what to do with the scripts, where I'd get the prompt, and what the dry run is is not clear"*)** — the sketch now does this; build it as shown:
- **Step 2 suggests a PRACTICE BATCH of 60** (two pieces) *"to learn the path, then go to 500"*, and says **where the file lands** (*your Downloads folder*).
- **Step 3 is three parts, each stating WHERE you do it:** **A** cut the file into pieces — *a terminal (PowerShell) opened in the draft folder*; the command uses the **Downloads path**; it explains **what the command makes** (a folder `data/enrichment-chunks/<date-time>/` with N pieces and `PROMPT.txt`) and to **keep the printed path** · **B** have a model fill each piece — *a chat with a model, NOT inside draft*; numbered sub-steps (open the piece, paste the instructions first, then the piece, save the reply as `chunk-001.filled.jsonl` in the same folder, repeat N times) · **C** join the pieces — the same terminal; it explains the **report** and **`redo.jsonl`**.

The earlier default was wrong and unmeasured.)* ⛔ **Before any truncation is ever offered, MEASURE it:** *what share of postings have their requirements section beyond character 3,000 and 6,000?* — and if it is then offered, **a posting cut short is flagged `truncated`, the prompt says *"if the text ends abruptly, fill only what you can see"*, and the dry run reports how many rows were filled from cut text.** *The pieces are small enough without it: 30 postings is about 40k tokens, well inside a chat.*

(5) **STOP — do not Apply.** (6) **Send back:** screenshots of steps 3 and 4 and **three notes: how long it took, where you hesitated, and anything the screen did not explain.**

The owner: *"we did manual runs to add companies — have we established an automated sweep at frequent intervals for the jobs to be rejuvenated, and can these discovery runs be added to those sweeps, automated or semi-automated? They need to run frequently. Should I run the SerpApi run now?"*

⭐ **STATUS 10-08 (38o): D78's age limit and CS scope are ENFORCED (both = 1, owner 10-08); the cron table is being confirmed by the D82 A lane** — **WHAT IS AUTOMATED TODAY** *(read from `server.js`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the log — ⛔ the agent confirms the exact cron table; I found the schedule only by reference)*: **ONE crawl of the configured companies a day, ~04:00 UTC** (new and changed postings upserted; a posting absent from **two consecutive** crawls is retired) · a 03:00 expired-jobs cleanup · the daily backup · the nightly ATS term-weight refresh · a board-fit pass after the crawl · the Draft House bin purge every 6 h · **D75's schedule tick every 5 minutes** (it only enqueues; it starts **paused and dry**) · **D78's age limit and CS scope are SWITCHES (`146_board_policy`) the owner must turn on.**
**NOT AUTOMATED:** (1) **company discovery** — HN and SerpApi are manual by design (D20: *"nothing schedules it"*); (2) **a more frequent crawl** — D74 P2 (adaptive cadence, retire on time not count) is **not evidenced as built.**

**THE LOOP, end to end — every stage a scheduled job, the owner a reviewer:**
```
DISCOVER  HN weekly · SerpApi daily (8, capped) · J1 board-finder daily
   → POOL  `company_candidates` (source, evidence, first / last seen)
   → PROBE  nightly, read-only, 25 at a time  (D80 A: in-scope roles, % ≤ 120d, US %, description %)
   → REVIEW  Admin → Companies → Candidates — ranked table; the owner approves in batches
   → ADD     backup · disk gate · D80 evidence record · reversible
   → CRAWL   configured companies, several times a day
   → HEAT    weekly: dormant / dead companies PROPOSED for deactivation (D80 E)
```

**A · THE CRAWL CADENCE — D74 P2, now concrete.** ⛔ **Report first (read-only):** the exact crons, and **each crawl's duration per source** — *a longer crawl is a cost, and 400 companies is not 20.* Then: **2 crawls a day to start (~04:00 and ~16:00 UTC), 4 (~every 6 h) once the duration and the disk allow**, polling **companies that posted this week more often than silent ones.** ⛔ **The retire rule becomes a TIME, not a count** (absent from two *successful* crawls **and** ≥ 48 h) — *with 4 crawls a day, two missed crawls would otherwise retire a live posting after twelve hours of a brief outage.* **Freshness target: median lag from posting to first sight < 6 h (D74).**

**B · THE DISCOVERY JOBS — server-side, no browser, no model (D17):**

- **SerpApi, daily, capped at 8** (D81's plan) — ⛔ **a RECORDED DELIBERATE REVERSAL of D20's "nothing schedules it"** — *what changed:* the sweep **only reads and pools**, the **cap and the quota check are unchanged** (an unreadable quota still refuses), and **adding a company still needs an approval.* Free plan: 8 a day is 240 of 250.
- **J1 board-finder, daily** — D75's schedule: **N tasks a day** from `need_board_discovery*.csv`, **dry-run first, then live** once the safety tests pass.

**C · THE POOL AND THE AUTO-PROBE.** One table, `company_candidates` (`source`, `evidence_json`, `status`: new → probed → approved / rejected → added / dormant, `first_seen`, `last_seen`), fed by all three. **A nightly job probes `new` rows read-only (25 a night, ≤ 1 request a second per host),** stores the numbers, and **ranks.** **Admin shows the D80 review table;** *Approve / Reject* act on a batch. ⛔ **Dedup against configured, held and rejected companies;** ⛔ **never a portfolio / VC board; never a deny-listed host.**

- **L2 — after ~4 weeks, if the owner approved ≥ 80% of what the table ranked highest:** **auto-add companies that clear a STRICT bar** (proposed: ≥ 10 in-scope roles, ≥ 60% of them ≤ 120 days, ≥ 70% US, 100% described) **under a weekly cap (≤ 15), the disk gate, a Draft-House-style banner and a 7-day veto, with one-click revert of the whole batch.**

**WHY IT IS WORTH ADDING NOW.** Google Jobs returns a company **because it has a live posting at that moment** — the strongest hiring signal there is, and **the only source that names companies on the big boards and Workday** (D4: 25 of the first 50 harvested pairs were Workday). **HN is saturated** (D80); the curated pool is a list, not a signal.

## ⛔⛔ D80 · WHICH COMPANIES — selected by evidence of active hiring, never by list membership — 2026-10-09

The owner, on the agent's first tranche of 25: *"why would the agent pick them — we don't even know if these companies are hiring. We need companies actively in the market with good postings out. This can be done via a manual session — I can start a manual session into one of the ATS pages like Workday, Indeed or LinkedIn and have the agent do the planned sweep of board URLs. 25 random companies won't cut it."* ⛔ **The owner is right, and the gap was mine:** D74 P3 and D78 D said *"validated on add — live, non-empty, description coverage, US evidence."* **Liveness is not hiring activity**, and the row never asked for recency or quality, so the agent followed it. The probe did show the 25 boards are **large (2,981 postings, 1,411 in scope)** — but **nothing about how recent or good they are**, because Greenhouse's dates are not trustworthy until a crawl re-dates them.

**THE PRINCIPLE:** a company enters the board **when its own board shows it is hiring NOW for CS roles, with postings worth showing** — and **the owner approves the list; the agent never picks it.**

### A · THE HIRING-EVIDENCE PROBE — read-only, per candidate (`scripts/companyProbe.mjs`)
- From the company's **own public board** (the same endpoints the adapters use), **one request, plus a sample of up to 10 postings for the true publish date**: **open postings** · **in-scope (CS) postings** (D78 B) · **share posted ≤ 30 / 60 / 120 days** · **median age** · **new in the last 30 days** · **description coverage** · **US share** · **salary stated %** (a quality signal) · a **sample of titles**.
- ⛔ **Dates:** use the field that means *published* (Lever `createdAt`, Ashby `publishedAt`, Greenhouse `first_published` from the posting itself — **not** `updated_at`); where none is trustworthy, **say so and admit the company only on probation** (below).
- **PROPOSED bar — the owner sets it:** **≥ 5 in-scope postings · ≥ 40% of them ≤ 120 days · ≥ 90% with a description · ≥ 50% US.** Companies are **ranked by fresh in-scope postings, capped, weighted by recency** — so a board with 8 recent roles outranks one with 200 stale ones.
- **PROBATION (optional, for untrusted dates):** crawl the company **hidden from the board for 7 days**; **promote only if it produced new in-scope postings.**

### B · WHERE CANDIDATES COME FROM — non-ToS only, strongest signal first
1. **Demand** — captures from companies we do not crawl (`hims-and-hers` is one), the companies users star or draft that we lack, and **"add a company" requests.** *A real person cared.*
2. **Live-posting sweeps (licensed)** — **SerpApi Google Jobs**, one search per role family × location. **A company's apply link appears because it has a live posting right now**; **rank by the number of distinct searches it appears in** — *a company in six searches is hiring in volume.* ⛔ **A pool, not a pairing** (D20); free plan 250 searches/month — **a paid tier is a budget decision for the owner.**
3. **HN *"Ask HN: Who is hiring?"*** — the monthly thread, via its public API: employers **posting this month**, usually with direct board links; **also slug discovery.**
4. **Reputable lists as POOLS only** — the ~2,200 known slugs, YC and well-known tech lists. **Membership is never a reason to admit; the probe decides.**
5. **Exclusions:** companies with **a large layoff in the last 90 days** (hold) · **staffing and recruiting agencies** (*"confidential employer"* postings) · duplicates of a configured employer · the **deny-list** (D75).

### C · THE ATTENDED SWEEP — the owner's idea, done safely
- **What it is:** the owner opens a page in **their own Chrome**; **the agent reads it** through the browser-control tools and writes **company names and board URLs to a candidates file** — **never to production**, and **every URL visited is logged.** The owner watches and can stop it. *It rides on the same idea as the extension's "read this page" — attended, never on page load.*
- ✅ **Pages it suits:** a Workday employer's **public** job site (to find the tenant and site name and read its open-role count) · startup and YC directories · the HN thread · funding round-ups · a company's own `/careers` · ATS board pages.
- ⛔ **NOT LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter or any site whose terms forbid automated access — even from the owner's own logged-in session.** **The violation is the automation, not the login;** it risks the owner's account, and **D75's deny-list already names them.** *Their postings are already reachable lawfully through Google Jobs (above).*
- ⛔ **Use a SEPARATE, clean Chrome profile with no logins.** The browser-control tools see every tab and cookie of the profile they drive; **never the owner's everyday profile.**
- ⚠ **FOUND 10-09: the browser-control tool is macOS-only** — it failed with `spawn osascript ENOENT` on the owner's Windows machine. **On Windows the attended sweep is a console script the OWNER runs in the clean profile, which downloads a CSV that the owner gives the agent** — *the same attended rule, and nothing remote-controls the owner's browser.* **First script: `hn_sweep.js`** (HN *"Who is hiring?"*, the last four monthly threads, the public Algolia API — **4 requests, spaced**; the parsing core is pure and **tested offline on 23 cases**). **Output `hn_candidates.csv`:** company · months hiring · ATS slug · site · remote · US hint · header, with the **request log as `#` lines at the end.** ⛔ **It keeps CS-looking, not-clearly-non-US posts only; the probe and the US gate decide the rest.** *Later seeds follow the same pattern.*
- ✅ **SECOND SWEEP, `hn_sweep2.js` (10-09)** — the same console workflow on `hn.algolia.com`, **13 requests**: **(1) the last 12 monthly *Who is hiring?* threads** (companies that post month after month are hiring steadily) and **(2) HN's own JOBS feed** — the *"X (YC S22) is hiring"* ads YC posts for its startups, **the same companies a YC directory scrape would reach, through an official public API.** Output `hn_candidates_v2.csv`: **company · sources · `n_months` · `recent4`** (months seen in the latest four) **· last month · YC batch · ATS · site · remote · US hint.** Tested offline on **35 cases** (the core is shared with the first script); a bug the tests caught: *a `ycombinator.com/companies` page is a profile, not a job board, and must not be reported as an ATS link.* **The agent diffs it against the first CSV and the configured list before anything is probed.**
- ⛔ **CONSIDERED AND DECLINED (so nobody re-proposes them):** **Remotive** — its API terms require attribution, **forbid passing its jobs to other sites**, delay listings 24 h and cap fetches at ~4 a day; it adds almost nothing a company-discovery pass can't already get. **RemoteOK** — attribution-bound with the same redistribution limits. **YC's company-directory search index** — reached with a key the page itself carries; its terms are unclear, and **HN's jobs feed already carries the same companies.** **Work at a Startup** — login-gated, terms restrict automated access.
- **Workday specifically:** tenant sites are public (`{tenant}.wd{n}.myworkdayjobs.com/{site}`); the sweep's value is **finding the tenant + site and counting open roles.** ⚠ The adapter's **300-posting cap and title filter** stay the limit (D74 P3) — a big employer's board is only partly readable.

### D · THE REVIEW TABLE → THE OWNER APPROVES
Columns: **company · vendor / slug · in-scope open roles · % ≤ 30 / 120 days · median age · salary % · US % · how it was found · title sample · exclusions hit.** The owner ticks; **the tranche is the approved list.** ⛔ **The evidence is stored with the company** (`company_ats_list` note): *"added 10-12 — 34 in-scope postings, 82% ≤ 120d, in 6 searches"* — **so any company's presence can be explained.** The scope enforcement and each add keep the **disk gate** and **dry-run-first.**

### E · THE LOOP — a list is maintained, not imported
**Weekly "hiring heat" per configured company.** **No new in-scope posting in 60 days = dormant**; **a 404 = dead** (distinguished); **the agent PROPOSES deactivation visibly and reversibly**, the owner approves. **Target: ≥ 80% of configured companies show a new in-scope posting in the last 30 days.** Companies that stop hiring leave the board.

### F · THE 25 ALREADY CHOSEN
✅ **APPROVED BY THE OWNER 10-09 (*"I approved the 25 companies — we need volume"*).** ⛔ **So the approval is the owner's, which is the rule D80 sets — the agent no longer waits on the probe for THESE 25.** They are the top 25 by CS yield from `d78TrancheProbe` (7,134 fetched → 2,981 pass US + age + classifier → 1,411 CS), **large, dated and 100% described.** ⚠ **Recency and quality are still unmeasured**; run the probe on them **anyway, after the add**, and **flag any that show none recent** — *they can be switched off.* **Every add passes the disk gate, and the apply script still checks each board is live.** ⛔ **Production writes stay the owner's** (the agent's shell writes are blocked): the owner runs the script, or uses **Admin → Ops → *Enforce CS scope*, *Run the scope sweep now*, then Admin → Companies.** **Scope enforcement and the 25 go in the SAME run** (below).

## ⛔⛔ D79 · THE APPLY WORKER — how auto-apply runs for users, and a spike before the system — 2026-10-09

✅ Owner 10-09: *"how is the VM deployed for users, for the auto apply pipeline — how are we going to design it, back end and front end"* — **"write it up."** **The design is `docs/APPLY_WORKER.md` — read it first.** It **supersedes the capture half of `VM_EXECUTION.md` V2** (no extension capture) and builds on E3 (**still unreviewed — O12**).

**IN SIX LINES:**
1. ⛔ **Users do not get a VM.** A user gets **an encrypted session per portal, stored as data**; **a shared worker** opens a fresh browser, loads it, fills the form, **stops at Review**, and discards the browser. It exists for the `gated` / `account` tier (~5% of the board) and is **the only route to mobile auto-apply.**
2. **Three trust zones, never one project:** **draft** (holds ciphertext it cannot read) · **the crawler** (D75, no secrets) · **the apply worker** (the only thing that decrypts), in **its own Railway workspace or a VPS**, with **no database credentials**, talking to draft over a narrow signed API.
3. ⭐ **THE KEY DESIGN:** the worker has a **signing identity pinned in the Android app**; for each connect it **mints a per-session encryption key and signs it**; **the app seals the session to it before upload**; **draft stores ciphertext only**; **revoke = the worker destroys that key, so the data becomes unreadable immediately, backups included.** *The older design let a compromised draft read sessions as they arrived.*
4. **Attended, always, until the gate:** the worker fills and **stops at Review**; **the user approves the VALUES** (a field list, **never a screenshot** of a signed-in page); on approval the worker **refills, verifies every value matches, and submits.** **UNATTENDED IS LOCKED** until O73 and a supervised full-auto run pass and **the kill switch is proven mid-batch on this path.**
5. **Front end:** **Settings → Portals you are signed in to** (D22) · **Draft House** gains *Ready to approve* and the expired-session *Stopped* card · **connecting happens in the Android app** (an in-app browser to the portal's own sign-in); **desktop keeps the gated handoff** — so **the extension needs no `cookies` permission and its listing does not change.**
6. ⛔ **What could kill it, answered before building:** **each portal's terms on automated submission** (Workday, Meta, Amazon — a per-platform fact; counsel agenda) · **session binding / datacenter IPs** (a phone-captured session replayed from a datacenter) · O12 unread · the Android app is early.

**⭐ STEP ONE IS A SPIKE, NOT THE SYSTEM** — *nothing uploaded to draft, nothing submitted, no key service, no worker project:*
- **S0.1** read **one portal's terms** on automated access → *forbid = stop.* **S0.2** `scripts/spikeCaptureSession.mjs` — a **headed** browser on the owner's machine, **the owner signs in themselves**, cookies + localStorage for that origin saved to a **passphrase-encrypted file outside the repo.** **S0.3 replay it** — same IP, then **a datacenter box (Railway's free throwaway VM, `ssh railway.new`)** — then **delete the box and sign out in the portal.** **S0.4** run the **existing fill** against a real application page **up to Review — do not press Submit.** **S0.5** a **go / no-go matrix.**
- ⚠ **Use a secondary account if one exists** — an automated session can get an account challenged. *Suggested first portal: Amazon (a single account at `account.amazon.jobs`, and the two-origin case D56 already met).*

**AFTER A GO:** P1 the key service and per-session sealing · P2 the worker and the lease API · P3 the Android connect flow · P4 the approval card and push · **P5 an attended pilot on one portal, the owner's account, five applications** · P6 more portals, **each through V4** · **P7 unattended — only past the gate.**

⛔ **Also recorded:** `/api/apply/session/*` returns **410** — **reversing it is a RECORDED DELIBERATE REVERSAL** (code, worklog, `CORRECTIONS_REGISTER.md`), stating *the password never passes through us and draft cannot read the session.* ⛔ **Disclosures that change together:** the **Play Store data-safety form**, the privacy policy, `PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION.md`, the in-app consent copy.

⛔ **THE OWNER DECIDES (doc §10):** **the first portal** and a secondary account · **the key service** (AWS / Google KMS — a new vendor) or **defer until the spike says GO** · **where the worker runs** (a separate Railway workspace or a VPS) · **push notifications** (the text must say *"a job is ready for your approval"* — never a company or a value) · **whether to keep this** if S0.1 or S0.3 says no — *the honest fallback is the gated handoff on desktop and no phone auto-apply.*

✅ **THE PORTALS SURFACE — DECIDED 10-09** *(supersedes D22's placement and this row's Settings placement; the full spec is `APPLY_WORKER.md` §6b; the layout is the sketch `portals-draft-house.html` — build to the file, not this prose)*:
- **Portals live in DRAFT HOUSE, not Settings.** A **Portals** box in the run bar — **plain when all is well, a mark (`1 expired` / `1 ending`) only when something needs the user** — opens **a drawer on desktop and a bottom sheet on Android, the same component.** **A Stopped card's *Reconnect* opens it with that portal already expanded.** **Settings keeps ONE pointer row** (*"3 connected · 1 expired — managed in Draft House"* + *Open in Draft House*) — **no second copy of the cards.**
- **The card is plain: a logo and a name; exceptions only as marks.** It expands in place (a real `<button>` with `aria-expanded`) to **the host · a time bar with the portal's own date · the use log · the actions.** ⛔ **Connect again renders ONLY on a dropped connection** (expired, or removed by the user); a healthy or expiring portal offers **Remove** only. **Remove** is an inline confirm and leaves **a dim, dashed record** (*key destroyed — unreadable since …*) **with its use log kept.**
- ⛔ **The general promise is said ONCE, above the cards:** *"**Sealed.** draft stores your signed-in session for each portal but cannot open it — only the apply worker can, while it runs your application. **Your password, card details and anything you type are never held.**"* The old per-card *Holds / Never holds* block is **gone.** · **Empty state:** says what a portal is, that **connecting happens in the Android app**, and that **on a computer draft borrows the browser session through the extension** — **no dead Connect button on desktop.**
- ⏸ **NOT YET CHOSEN** (recommendations in `sessions.html`): **the connect flow** (add a manual *"I'm signed in"* fallback) · **the approval screen** (B on the phone, C on desktop) · the notification text. ⛔ **No swipe-to-approve.**

⭐ **STATUS 10-08 (38o): PUSHED (`79a3bb0`)** — ✅ **S0.2 BUILT 10-08 (38k), local, unpushed** — `scripts/spikeCaptureSession.mjs` (HEADED, a throwaway profile deleted on exit; the owner signs in; it reads only the browser's cookies for the named origins and their localStorage — no form field, no keystroke, no upload) · `scripts/spikeReplaySession.mjs` (S0.3: a fresh browser, headless by default, ONE page; prints *SESSION SURVIVED / SIGNED OUT / CHALLENGED* with the landed host + path — no screenshot, no page text, no value) · `scripts/spikeSession.mjs` (sealed with services/secretBox.js under a scrypt key from a passphrase typed with echo off — never argv; ⛔ the file is refused inside this repo AND inside any git work tree). `C:Usersduggidraft-secrets` passes the guard. +7 tests, mutations red; suite **3840 / 3840 / 0**. ⛔ **The owner runs it** — after S0.1 (the portal's terms) and with a secondary account if one exists:
`node scripts/spikeCaptureSession.mjs --url <portal sign-in page> --out C:Usersduggidraft-secretsspike<portal>.session` → `node scripts/spikeReplaySession.mjs --in <that file> --url <a signed-in page>` → then on a throwaway datacenter box → delete the box, sign out in the portal.

**AGENT, NOW:** only **S0.2** — write `scripts/spikeCaptureSession.mjs` (headed, owner signs in, passphrase-encrypted output outside the repo, refuses a destination inside the repo, never reads a password field) and the replay script. ⛔ **Nothing else in this row is built until the spike reports.**

- ⛔ **At INGEST:** a posting whose `posted_at` is older than 120 days is **not written** — logged to `rejected_jobs` as `too_old`. ⛔ **A NULL date is never a reason to drop** — fall back to `first_seen`. ⚠ **Report which date each adapter actually supplies** (*first published* vs *last updated*) and how many are NULL — an `updated_at` makes an old posting look fresh, so *"120 days" is only as honest as the field.* This also **slows the volume's growth.**
