### ✅ P1 (part) · THE CLASSIFIER FIX — BUILT 10-07 (38g) on the owner's *"fix the classifier"* — ⭐ PUSHED and LIVE (38g, `24063c8`)

Measured on ONE fixed live fetch of the 20 boards (2,671 US-admitted postings, `scripts/d74DropSample.mjs --save-fetch`), diffed before/after with `scripts/d74ClassifierDiff.mjs`: **drops 765 → 424 (341 rescued: sales 87 · finance 71 · marketing 61 · hr 29 · data 25 · pm 21 · operations 20 · legal 15 · design 10 · engineering 2) · 0 newly dropped · 52 kept postings moved — every one from `general` (invisible on every board) to a real family (30-odd "Research Engineer" → data, HRIS → hr, payroll → finance) · 0 moved between two real families.** Precision of the rescued, read title by title: ~4 questionable of 341 (*"Executive Assistant, Growth Marketing"* → marketing, *"Policy Design Manager"* → design).
- **Why they dropped:** the right family scored only as a weak hint (0.35) and the 0.75 rule drops anything without a strong anchor. Three causes — **inverted order** (*"Manager, Customer Success"* never contains *"customer success manager"*), **noun forms** (*Product Management · Strategic Finance · Revenue Accounting · Sales Development · Product Marketing*), **missing terms** (*sourcer · RE / RS · post-training · economist*).
- **The fix:** `D74_STRONG_ANCHORS` in `services/jobClassifier.js` — one block, provenance in its comment, appended to each family's strong anchors. ⭐ **The first draft collided ten times** (`treasury`, `recruiting`, `procurement`, `accounting`, `product operations`, `sales strategy`, `marketing analytics`, `, tax`): a phrase two families claim scores *ambiguous* (0.55) and **drops** the title — it took *"Product Manager, Treasury for Platforms"* off the board. Each was narrowed until the diff read **0 newly dropped**; the ten are now regression tests.
- **Stored rows:** a re-crawl skips an unchanged posting, so the dropped ones arrive on the next 08:00 crawl by themselves, but rows already filed under `general` would stay there. `services/jobs/remapGeneralRoles.js` re-files them at boot — **classifier rows only** (`source_profile_id IS NULL`), only to a family `classifyJob` now names, one transaction, **reversible** by `matched_by = 'd74_remap_general'`. Kept OUT of `backfillRoleMap.js`, which a guard holds to INSERT-only.
- **Tests:** `test/d74ClassifierAnchors.test.js` — 25 rescued titles reach their family · the 10 collisions stay put · **no strong anchor is shared by two families** · the re-file moves classifier rows only, once, and a dry run writes nothing (red with the anchors disabled). `npm test` **3791 / 3791 / 0**. ⚠ `server.js` was briefly converted to LF by a `sed -i` this session and restored to CRLF before any commit (the byte-identity tests pass).

### THE PLAN — each phase gated by P0's numbers

**P1 · STOP THE LEAKS (no new sources, no new spend).**
- ⭐ **Make a new posting scoreable the moment it lands** — deterministic term extraction over `description_text` at ingest (D72 P1/P2), so **fresh jobs are not buried.** *Likely the highest-leverage change on this page, because it removes the dependence on a manual sweep for the newest rows.*
- **The discard audit → fix the classifier** where it drops good rows. At a 30% discard rate, even a modest false-drop rate is a double-digit gain **at zero crawl cost.**
- **Dead slugs:** auto-deactivate **visibly and reversibly**; 404 vs empty; the 48h health threshold re-checked.
- **"New since your last visit"** on `first_seen`, not the company's posted date — the lens a daily product needs.
- **Workday / SmartRecruiters:** settle the two notions of "configured".

**P2 · CADENCE.** The ATS boards are public JSON; polling them more often is cheap. **Adaptive per company** — a board that posted this week is polled more than one that has been silent for a month; **ETag / If-Modified-Since where the vendor supports it.** ⛔ **Retire on a TIME, not a count** (e.g. absent from two *successful* crawls **and** ≥ 48h). Show the **crawl age** in Admin.

**P3 · VOLUME — add companies, in tranches, measured.**
- **Seed from the ~2,200-company curated lists**, **validated on add** (live, non-empty, **description coverage — never 0%**, US evidence) — `validateBoard` already refuses `no_descriptions` (D20).
- **Tranche of 25 first**, measure **rows per company, US-relevant yield, MB per row**, extrapolate, then **~100 a week.** ⚠ **Order of magnitude, not a promise:** boards run from a handful to hundreds of postings; after the role, US and dedup filters, only a fraction is relevant.
- **The other discovery channels, already built:** D20's SerpApi sweep (**≈ 2 new pairs per search, falling**), extension captures (D33/D64), and a user "add a company" request.
- **Workday is its own project:** the tenant site must be parsed from the URL, and the adapter **caps at 300 postings with a title filter** — poor for the big boards. D4 found **25 of 50 harvested pairs were Workday**; it is where large employers live.
- ⛔ **Gate every tranche on storage and on the A49 dedup**, not only on enrichment — *enrichment is no longer the throttle if P1's deterministic scoring lands.*

**P4 · NEW FEEDS — each a decision, each through the same gates** (US gate, relevance, dedup tier, description coverage, direct-apply):
- **Jobo:** a **bounded paid test** — fund a small wallet, measure **unique** postings (not already on a direct ATS), direct-apply fraction and US share. *~3 credits per posting; the default batch is a free-tier 10.* ⛔ A bounded experiment, never an open tap.
- **Free remote and community feeds** (Remotive, RemoteOK, We Work Remotely, the monthly *Who is hiring*) — mostly **direct links to ATS boards**, so they are **also slug discovery.**
- ⛔ **Not USAJobs** — federal roles require citizenship (D59's HARD class).

**TARGETS — *proposed; the owner sets them*:** **~150–300 companies · ~8–15k active US-relevant rows · ≥ 60 new relevant US postings a day · median lag from posting to first sight < 6h · ≥ 90% of new rows scoreable at first sight · the share of rows older than 60 days falling.** ⚠ These assume the board stays **engineering-only** — widening the role scope changes every number.

✅ **DECIDED BY THE OWNER 10-09 (supersedes this line):** **target ~300 companies with a MUCH STRICTER filter** · **posted within 120 days** · **Jobo RETIRED** (we run our own crawls) · **old postings are REMOVED, not hidden or dimmed** — *no 60-day dim* — **unless the user applies for them** · **computer science only — not widened.** **The build row is D78.**

## ⛔ D73 · EMAIL — three streams on one domain: the owner's mail, service mail, and (later) promotions — 2026-10-08

> ✅ **§A DONE BY THE OWNER (10-09) · §B BUILT 10-09 (39a) — `b1bd07c`, LOCAL.** All seven items; `test/d73Email.test.js` covers the row's ⛔ list (8 tests, each guard mutation-checked). Webhook scheme verified from Resend's and Svix's docs (HMAC-SHA256 over `id.timestamp.rawBody`, `whsec_` base64 secret, `v1,` signatures; events `email.bounced` — Permanent suppresses — and `email.complained`, recipients in `data.to`). ⏸ The owner: `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` + the webhook in Resend (O90 b). ⛔ **No promotional send path** — the marketing sender is tested and imported by nothing; it needs `MARKETING_SENDS_ENABLED` and `MAIL_POSTAL_ADDRESS` (the owner's, O90 f).

✅ Owner 10-08: DNS is already on **Cloudflare**; Resend has not been set up. Wanted: **a personal address at the company domain (`yellela.s@`)**, other required addresses, **and a way to send updates, policy notices and (later) promotions to users.** *"That's it for now apart from other required ones."*

**THE THREE STREAMS** — each has a different best tool; they share one domain and must not share one sender:

| Stream | Tool | Address |
|---|---|---|
| **The owner's / developers' mail** | **Cloudflare Email Routing** to receive → **Gmail "Send mail as" through Resend SMTP** to send | `yellela.s@` · `privacy@` · `support@` · `dmarc@` · `postmaster@` · `abuse@` |
| **Service mail** — reset codes, verification, **policy and terms notices** | **Resend API** (`services/emailService.js` already calls it) | `Draft <noreply@jobsviadraft.com>` |
| **Promotions and product news** | **Resend Broadcasts**, from a **separate subdomain**, **opt-in only** | **not yet — no sends until there are users and §B exists** |

⛔ **No catch-all** (it invites spam). `noreply@` has **no inbox**; transactional mail carries a **`Reply-To: support@`** so a reply goes somewhere. Cloudflare's forwarding is **not a mailbox** — when a second developer needs a real one, move to a hosted mailbox, **and only one provider may own the inbound MX records.**

### §A · OWNER STEPS, in this order (the agent cannot reach Cloudflare, Resend or Gmail)

1. **Cloudflare → Email Routing → enable** (it adds its own MX + SPF). Create the six addresses above, each **forwarding to the owner's Gmail**; verify the destination from the email Cloudflare sends.
2. **Resend → add the domain `jobsviadraft.com`.** Use its Cloudflare auto-setup if offered, then **read what it added**; otherwise copy the records it shows into Cloudflare DNS, **proxy OFF (grey cloud)**. Expect DKIM at `resend._domainkey`, and SPF + MX on a **`send` subdomain** — *from memory; trust what Resend displays.* ⛔ **One SPF record per hostname.** Railway's records stay **DNS-only** too.
3. **DMARC:** a TXT at `_dmarc` → `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@jobsviadraft.com`. **Start at `p=none`; tighten to `quarantine` after two to four weeks of clean reports.**
4. **Two Resend API keys** — one for the app, one for Gmail — so a leak from one place does not expose the other. ⛔ **Never paste a key into chat or a file in the repo.**
5. **Gmail → Settings → Accounts → Send mail as** → `yellela.s@jobsviadraft.com` (and optionally `support@` / `privacy@`, so replies leave from them) via Resend's SMTP (`smtp.resend.com`, user `resend`, password = the Gmail key; **check Resend's docs for ports**). Gmail's verification code reaches you through step 1's forwarding.
6. **Railway (draft service):** `RESEND_API_KEY` = the app key · `EMAIL_FROM` = `Draft <noreply@jobsviadraft.com>` · ⚠ **check `PASSWORD_RESET_FROM`** — it outranks the default and a stale value breaks sending. **Batch with the other pending variable changes** (each change restarts production).
7. **Test:** *forgot password* to yourself → Gmail's **Show original** → **SPF, DKIM and DMARC all `pass`** → send one reply from `yellela.s@`.
8. ⚠ **Check Resend's CURRENT free limits** (emails per day, verified domains). If the free plan allows one domain, the marketing subdomain waits.
9. **Chrome Web Store:** list **`support@`** as the support contact and **verify the developer contact email** — the reviewer sees both, and **`privacy@` is already published in the policy.**

**Resume Master (`resumemaster.one`) is out of scope for now** — no users, and its own `passwordReset: false` blocks nothing.

### §B · APP WORK — agent, once §A step 6 is done (all of it deterministic; no model call)

1. **`sendEmail` grows up:** `html`, `headers`, `reply_to` (currently `to`, `subject`, `text` only). **Transactional stays plain text.** New constant `SUPPORT_EMAIL` in `shared/brand.js` beside `PRIVACY_CONTACT_EMAIL` and `SENDER_EMAIL` — *"derive from here; do not decide per-file."* ⛔ **Production's `EMAIL_FROM` still overrides the default — test it.**
2. **Consent, stored honestly:** `marketing_opt_in` · `marketing_opt_in_at` · `marketing_opt_in_source` · `unsubscribed_at`. ⛔ **A signup checkbox, OFF by default.** Never inferred, never bundled with accepting the terms. **Capture it correctly from the first signup — retrofitting means asking everyone again.**
3. **One-click unsubscribe:** a **signed-token route** that works **without logging in** and is **idempotent**, **plus** the `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers on every marketing send (Gmail and Yahoo require them of bulk senders).
4. **Bounces and complaints:** a **Resend webhook** (`bounced`, `complained`) into a **suppression table** — **signature-verified, raw body**, secret `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — and **nothing is ever sent to a suppressed address.** ⚠ Confirm the exact event names and signing scheme from Resend's docs.
5. **Admin → "Send a notice" — for policy, terms and service notices:** an **audience**, a **dry run that shows the recipient count first**, a **hard ceiling** that refuses past it unless explicitly raised, a **test-to-me** mode, **provider rate limits respected**, and a **log of who / when / how many** (not the message content). ⛔ **It carries the same brake the 1,288-row deletion lacked.** Notices are **service messages** — no opt-in needed — and say why the user is receiving them.
6. **Marketing footer:** an **unsubscribe link and a postal address** in every promotional message — ⛔ the address is **an env var (`MAIL_POSTAL_ADDRESS`), never committed**, and it must be **a PO box or a registered-agent address, not a home address.** ⛔ **No promotional send is built or enabled** until the owner says so.
7. **Disclosure:** **Resend receives user email addresses and message content** — a row in the privacy policy and in `PRIVACY_RECONCILIATION`; the policy states the marketing consent, how to withdraw it, and that service notices are separate. **Cloudflare carries inbound mail to the published contact addresses** — reconcile whether the policy should say so.

⛔ **Tests (each red when removed):** a reset email still sends to a user who unsubscribed from marketing · a marketing send **skips** an unsubscribed or suppressed address · the unsubscribe route works signed-out and twice · a webhook with a **bad signature is refused** · the notice tool **refuses above its ceiling** and its dry run **sends nothing** · `Reply-To` is `support@` on service mail · **no promotional sending path is reachable.**

⛔ **THE OWNER DECIDES:** the **postal address** for marketing footers (PO box or registered agent) · whether `support@` should send *from* itself too · when a second developer gets a hosted mailbox.

## ⛔⛔ D72 · THE TAGGING STRATEGY — one tag layer, read by everything — 2026-10-08

✅ Owner 10-08: *"we need to tag everything within a posting and résumé properly, so that we can control it. This is the one thing that will make or break this."* **The strategy is `docs/TAGGING_STRATEGY.md` — read it first; this row is the build order.**

**THE IDEA IN SIX LINES:**
1. **Three subjects, one vocabulary** — the **posting**, the **candidate**, and the **form question** (so autofill maps *dimension → fact* exactly instead of guessing from wording).
2. **A tag is a claim with provenance:** `state` (stated / derived / **unknown**) · `source` · an **evidence span** in `description_text` · `tagger_version` · `text_hash`. ⛔ **`unknown` is not `no`; no default is ever a tag; the owner's tag wins and survives a re-tag.**
3. **A dimension registry** defines every dimension once, with a **class: HARD** (eligibility — *surfaced, never decided, never guessed, stated by the candidate and never read from résumé text*) · **SOFT** (ranking) · **INFO** · **BOILERPLATE** (excluded from scoring).
4. **A deterministic extraction ladder** per dimension — provider field → JSON-LD → label block → **trailing block (D71)** → prose pattern → vocabulary → **unknown** → the **owner's export → tag → import sweep.** ⛔ **No model call** (D17).
5. **Measurement gates the UI:** a gold set per dimension; **precision, recall and coverage**; a **readiness state** (*experimental → beta → ready*) that the dials, the sentence and the Requirements row **obey.** ⛔ *Coverage is not accuracy* — metro was 91.7% and Boston was still wrong.
6. **The vocabulary learns through a queue, never directly** — unknown terms ranked by frequency; the owner promotes in batches with the five guards, a batch row and a revert; **every vocabulary change bumps `tagger_version`, dry-runs the re-tag and re-measures ρ.**

◐ **P0 STARTED 10-07 (38g) — the inventory, the registry as data, and the measurement tools; measured on a MIGRATED COPY of the local board (2,613 active, 10-06 era); production waits on a push (the registry is not on it yet). No behaviour change.**
- 🚀 **PRODUCTION, measured 10-07 (38g) after `7f6e89b` went live** (`railway ssh … node scripts/d72P0Measure.mjs`, read-only; 1,942 active). **Coverage:** citizenship 100 *(read)* · clearance 100 *(read)* · sponsorship **1.1** · location_country 98.6 · location_place 89.0 · workstyle **61.6** *(greenhouse 47.1)* · level 72.8 · **years_required 0 stored** · function 75.7 · employment_type **7.5** · skills 94.1 · pay 78.1 *(after D71)* · posted_at 99.9 · apply_tier 99.9. **Owner-tagged rows: 0** — so no precision yet; every dimension `experimental (unmeasured)`.
  - **Level:** `tag_level` and `experience_level` disagree on **378 of 1,414 (27%)**; `experience_level = 'mid'` on 795, and on **506** that default is the only level on file.
  - **US:** `tag_us = non_us` on **31** active rows the gate admitted (the local copy's 711 was a pre-gate board — ⚠ that local figure is withdrawn). Still two verdicts that disagree, one unread.
  - **Defaults served:** `ghost_score = 0` and `collar = 'white'` on all 1,942 · `bucket_seniority = 'mid'` 1,009 · `bucket_domain = 'general'` 1,097. **Candidates: all 10 users read `requires_sponsorship = 0` with no `sponsorship_need` answer; all 10 `has_clearance = 0`; 9 of 11 job profiles sit at the `'mid'` default.**
  - ⭐ **THE GOLD SET IS EXPORTED from production's board** — `data/d72-gold/` on the agent's machine (gitignored; written to the container's `/tmp`, copied, deleted there): **10 files, 489 rows** (location_country 39: only 14 rows are unknown), a `README.txt` with each vocabulary. Grade the `gold` column (`none` = the posting does not state it); then `node scripts/d72P0Measure.mjs --gold data/d72-gold` gives precision and recall. Citizenship's file has 5 extracted rows and 45 unknown — 36 of those mention citizenship or export-control words, which is where a miss would be.
- **The registry:** `shared/tagRegistry.js` — **33 dimensions** (20 posting · 9 candidate · 2 question + 2 inventory rows), each with its proposed class, every store it lives in today (with `role`: primary / legacy / copy / unread / dead), writers, readers and **how unknown is stored**. `test/d72TagRegistry.test.js` holds it to the schema: every column it names exists, and **every tag-like column on `scraped_jobs` must be claimed** — it caught three gaps on its first run (`salary_max_usd`, the two `pay_text_*`, and `req_uid`, the dedup requisition id).
- **The tools:** `scripts/d72P0Measure.mjs` (coverage overall and by source · defaults posing as facts · drift between stores · precision vs the OWNER's own tags in `tag_owner_json` · precision/recall from graded gold files; `--copy` measures a migrated copy) and `scripts/d72GoldExport.mjs` (50 rows per dimension, **stratified: half the tagger filled, half it left unknown — and for a dimension with a hint, the unknown half leans on rows whose text uses its words**, because random unknowns of a rare HARD dimension are all true "none" and recall would read 100% while testing nothing). Writes to `data/d72-gold/` (gitignored). **Nothing is imported**; the measure reads the graded CSVs.
- **The local table (coverage only — precision/recall need the gold; production has 0 owner-tagged rows to compare against, ⚠ unverified until read):** citizenship 99.9 *(read; stated on 5 rows)* · clearance 99.9 *(read; stated on 32)* · sponsorship **0.3** · location_country 98.5 · location_place 65.5 · workstyle 44.3 · level 66.7 · **years_required 0 stored** · function 76.0 · employment_type **8.0** · skills 30.6 · pay 61.2 · posted_at 69.6 *(ashby 0)* · apply_tier 100. **Every dimension is `experimental (unmeasured)`** — coverage is not accuracy.
- ⭐ **PREMISES THE FIRST MEASUREMENT ALREADY OVERTURNS:**
  1. **Level has two answers on a third of the board:** `tag_level` and `experience_level` are both filled on 1,746 rows and **disagree on 610 (35%)** — and the yoe sorts (`jobCursor` LEVEL_RANK) and the panel's `experienceLevel` read `experience_level`, which `normalizeExperienceLevel` defaults to `'mid'` (1,247 rows; on **693** the default is the ONLY level on file).
  2. ~~⛔ **`tag_us` says `non_us` on 711 active rows**~~ — ⚠ **withdrawn: production reads 31** (the local copy predates the gate's retire pass). Still two verdicts that disagree, one of them unread.
  3. **The years filters and sorts read `min_years_exp`, which nothing writes** (0 rows) — the deck strip computes years from the text (1,331 rows have an ask) and nothing else uses it.
  4. **Defaults served as facts:** `ghost_score = 0` and `collar = 'white'` on every row (no writer), `bucket_seniority = 'mid'` 1,400, `bucket_domain = 'general'` 1,479; candidate side: `domain_profiles.seniority` NOT NULL DEFAULT `'mid'` (feeds the scorer's junior-posting cap), sponsorship and clearance copies DEFAULT 0 (`cleanStructuredFacts` coerces unknown to `false`).
  5. **Workstyle is 21% on Greenhouse** (84% Ashby, 100% Lever) — the dial's coverage is a per-source fact.
- **NEXT (the owner's):** ✅ pushed and measured on production (above) · **grade the gold** (§13.3; ~500 rows, 10 files — or say which dimensions a second reader may grade) · the §13 decisions before P1.

**BUILD ORDER — each phase has an exit test (strategy §12):**
- ⛔ **P0 · INVENTORY, REGISTRY, MEASUREMENT — FIRST, AND NOTHING ELSE UNTIL IT REPORTS.** Map **every tag-like field in the repo** (the `tag_*` columns, `job_tag_places`, `skills_json`, the label-block and pay parsers, D65's résumé parse, `domain_profiles`, the claims) to a dimension; **write the registry as data**; **measure coverage, precision and recall per dimension against a first gold set.** **No behaviour changes.** Report one table: *dimension · class · coverage · precision · recall · readiness.* ⚠ Expect the first measurement to **overturn a premise** — it has every time.
- **P1** provenance and spans (`posting_tags`, written **alongside** the old columns, with a parity test) · **P2** the vocabulary queue and sweep tooling · **P3** candidate tags with tiers and stable résumé bullet ids · **P4** question tags for the resolver · **P5** readiness gates and **Admin → Tags** · **P6** outcomes joined to tags.
- ⛔ **Strangler migration, not a rewrite:** `posting_tags` becomes the source of truth and the existing `tag_*` columns become its **materialised read model**, written only from it. Both runners, byte-identical.

**HOW THE OPEN ROWS FIT:** **D71** (pay and location in the prose) is **P0's first dimension fix** · **D42**'s precision / recall *is* P0's method · **D59**'s requirements are the HARD class · **D65** supplies the candidate side · **D70**'s keywords-only variant reads **evidenced + claimed** tags and needs **spans** (P1) · **D55**'s autofill needs **question tags** (P4).

⛔ **THE OWNER DECIDES (strategy §13) — before P1:** the **class of each dimension** · the **readiness thresholds** (proposed HARD ≥ 98%, SOFT ≥ 90%) · who **grades the gold sets** (~50 per dimension, in the existing export/import format) · **who promotes vocabulary** (proposed: the owner, in batches) · whether to adopt a **company-level `industry` dimension** · the **strangler** migration. **P0 needs none of these** — it only measures.

## ⛔ D71 · PAY AND LOCATION THAT SIT IN THE PROSE — the page says "not stated" about something the text states — 2026-10-08

The owner revisited a **captured Amazon posting**: its card and deck strip show **no location and no salary**, yet **the posting's own text says both, in plain sight at the very end:**

```
The base salary range for this position is listed below. …
USA, MA, Boston - 143,700.00 - 194,400.00 USD annually
```

⛔ **The panel is asserting *"not stated"* about a fact it holds.** That is the same class as the *"Not linked"* label and *"No signal" beside "Strong match"* — **a surface asserting what it could have checked.** It also means the Salary sort, the salary filter and the location filters (D42) all miss this job.

⚠ **Probable cause — the agent confirms it:** D59's label-block parser reads a **leading** run of `Label: value` lines; this fact is a **trailing** line in a different shape — **`<location> - <min> - <max> <ISO currency> <unit>`**, with **no `$`, `.00` decimals, a currency code AFTER the number, and `annually` as the unit.** A salary matcher built for `$150,000 – $180,000` will never see it.

**THE FIX — deterministic (D17), over the WHOLE description, not its head:**

1. **A pay-range parser over `description_text`.** It reads: a currency **symbol or an ISO code** (`USD`, before *or after* the numbers) · thousands separators and **decimals** (`143,700.00`) · the `k` suffix (`150k`) · any dash — hyphen, en, em — or `to` / `between X and Y` · a **unit**: `annually`, `per year`, `/yr`, `hourly`, `per hour`, `/hr`, `monthly`. Output: `min`, `max`, `currency`, `unit`, `source = 'description'`.
2. ⭐ **PAY IS OFTEN PER LOCATION.** Large employers list **one line per location, each with its own range** (`USA, CA, Palo Alto — 150,000 — 210,000 USD`, then `USA, WA, Seattle — …`). **Store each `(location, min, max)`** — D29 already models location as a set; **pay is per member of it.** Display one range as *$143.7k–$194.4k*; with several, the **overall min–max** on the card, the **per-location lines** in the panel (a muted second line, as Workstyle's location), and — when the user has filtered to a place — **that place's range.**
3. **The location comes from the same line.** `USA, MA, Boston` is **country, state, city** — Amazon's convention (their page header reads *US, MA, Boston*). Feed it to **D29's tags**: country **US = positive US evidence** (D41(d), so this capture is accepted), state **MA**, metro **Boston**. Also handle `Boston, MA, USA` and `Boston, MA`. ⛔ **D59's trap still applies:** a street name is not a city.
4. **Precedence, never an overwrite:** the provider's structured salary field → JSON-LD `baseSalary` → the leading label block (D59) → **this prose scan.** A structured value is never replaced; `source` is kept so the panel can say *"from the posting text"*; if two sources disagree materially, keep the structured one and note it.
5. ⛔ **"Not stated" is only shown after the WHOLE text was scanned**, and it is a different statement from *"couldn't read it"* (an empty or failed description). Never print the first when the truth is the second.
6. ⛔ **Hourly stays hourly** (*$45–$60 /hr*). Never convert silently; the Salary sort uses an explicit **annualised estimate, flagged as an estimate.**
7. ⛔ **False-positive traps — each a NEGATIVE test:** *"$10,000,000 in revenue"* · *"401(k) matching up to 6%"* · *"10–20 years of experience"* · *"a team of 143,700"* · *"$1–2 million budget"*. **A range counts as pay only with pay context** (*base pay, salary, compensation, pay range, annually, per hour*) **or** a currency plus a pay unit. A wrongly parsed salary is worse than a missing one.

🚀 **LIVE 10-07 (38g): `c0e0217` pushed on the owner's *"push it"*** — `/api/version` started 15:58:44Z, `latestApplied: 141_pay_from_text`, contract 2.4.0, `/api/health` 200. ✅ **Production acceptance, read after boot:** the owner's Amazon row carries pay **143,700–194,400** from the text, location **Boston, MA**, `tag_us = us`, place **MA / Boston** · every active row re-read (`v2`; 771 inactive left for the next 10-minute pass) · **250 of the 260 measured postings now carry a salary** (3 hourly); the rest are the detector's over-count or non-USD pay (kept in the fields, not in the USD sort columns). Was: ✅ **BUILT 10-07 (38g), local — migration 141, contract 2.4.0.** `services/jobs/payFromText.js` scans the WHOLE text (currency required, pay context or a pay unit required, plausibility per unit, *million/billion* refused, the place read from the same line — country/state/city either order, a street is not a city). It rides D59's pass: **`NORMALIZER_VERSION` 1 → 2**, so the boot pass re-reads every row (active first now), writes the text's pay into `description_fields.pay` (as stated, with `source` and per-location lines) and a **USD-per-year estimate** into the two new columns `pay_text_min_usd` / `pay_text_max_usd` for the salary **sort** and **filter** only — ⛔ the provider's `salary_*` are never written. Precedence: provider → label block → the text. `mapJobRow` drops normalizeJob's *"Location not specified"* placeholder for the label block's place or the pay line's; D29's tags take the pay line's place (Boston → MA + the metro → US). Display: ONE salary label (`shared/postingFacts.js` `salaryLabel`) now prints the card, deck, bubble and strip — **the card printed `USD144k→USD194k` for every USD salary**, and there were four copies — one decimal when it informs (*$143.7k*), hourly as *$45–$60 /hr*; the strip's salary cell says *from the posting text* or lists each place's range; *"couldn't read the posting"* replaces *"not stated"* only when there is no text. Contract **2.4.0**: `salaryPeriod`, `salarySource`, `payLocations`, `descriptionMissing` (additive). **Rehearsed on a `.backup()` copy of the local board (`scripts/d71Backfill.mjs`):** salary-empty active rows **1,253 → 999 (254 gained: 252 from the text, 2 from the label block; 251 annual, 3 hourly)**, ⛔ `description` + `content_hash` + every `salary_*` byte-identical; matched lines spot-checked (all *"salary range … $X – $Y"* shapes; the 3 hourly are hourly). 10 tests, each red with its source reverted. ⏸ **Production is re-read by the boot pass on deploy** (the script imports code production does not run yet) — the acceptance on the owner's Amazon row is the first thing to read after the push. ⚠ Not changed: the **5,000-char description cap** (76% of rows sit at it; a pay line past it is cut) — raising it rewrites `description` and therefore `content_hash`, which A76's grades key on: the owner's call.

◐ **MEASURED 10-07 (38g), on the owner's go — production and local** (`scripts/d71PayMeasure.mjs`, read-only, counts only; a deliberately simple detector — a numeric range with a pay word on its line or the line before — so it over-counts the traps slightly):

| | active | salary empty | ⭐ **pay in the text, salary empty** | at the 5,000-char cap | no location places |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **production** | 1,942 | 675 | ⭐ **260 (38.5% of the empty)** — greenhouse **258**, ashby 1, import 1 | 1,480 (76%) | 29 (greenhouse 26) |
| local copy | 2,613 | 1,253 | 258 — greenhouse 254, workable 3, ashby 1 | 1,854 | — (older schema) |

⭐ **It is not one posting: ~13% of production's board states pay that the board says is not stated, almost all Greenhouse** (whose structured `pay_input_ranges` is often absent while the description carries a pay-transparency section). Production holds **2 captured (import) rows, both salary-empty; 1 carries the Amazon-shape trailing line** — the owner's. ⚠ **76% of descriptions sit at the 5,000-character cap** (`htmlToText.js`), and pay lines are usually at the END — so the cap can cut off the very fact D71 reads; the parser must run on the longest text the row holds, and the count above is a **floor**.

**MEASURE, THEN BACKFILL — the D59 pattern:**
- **Count** the rows whose text contains a pay range and whose salary is NULL, **by source and by ATS**, and the same for location. Report it — that is the size of the problem, and it is probably not one posting.
- **Backfill into NEW columns**; ⛔ **`description` and `content_hash` stay byte-identical** (A76's grades and the enrichment imports are keyed on the hash). **Dry run first, with before/after pairs, a batch row and a revert**, as the enrichment path does.
- **Re-parse the owner's captures once** — the Amazon one must now read *Boston, MA* and *$143.7k–$194.4k* on the card, the deck strip and the posting panel.

✅ **Acceptance:** the Amazon posting shows **Boston, MA** and **$143.7k–$194.4k**; it appears under *in Boston* and under the US floor; it sorts by salary; and the count of *pay in the text, salary empty* **falls to the traps' false negatives only.** ⛔ **Fixtures:** the Amazon text (the line above, verbatim) · a **multi-location** posting · **hourly** · a **`k`-suffix** range · **`between X and Y`** · a `$` range with `per year` · and the five traps. **Tests (each red when removed):** the Amazon line parses · the multi-location lines yield several `(location, min, max)` · the traps do **not** parse · a structured salary is never overwritten · **`description` and `content_hash` are unchanged after the backfill.**

- **(4) `classify` does NOT run on draft's job path.** `generateRequest` always sends `roleFamily` when there is an active profile (`"general"` when unset — `services/toolsServiceRequests.js:54`), so Resume Master never classifies. - ⭐ **Found while building item 3 → A94: the ledger cannot tell a refusal from a delivery.** A claim-guard refusal is a model call that succeeded, so its row reads `success = 1`. Only the ATS columns separate them (the delivered path writes `ats_score_before` and fills `ats_score_after`; the catch path writes neither), so `d70LedgerRead.mjs` **infers** the outcome and says so. Phase 3's *"count them in the ledger by purpose"* needs a real marker first.
- ⭐ **WHAT IT SAYS — for the owner's decision:** (a) **the premise is refuted for dollars:** the description is ≤ 5.5% of a call, so keywords-instead-of-posting saves **≤ ~0.3¢**; Phase 1 stands only on fabrication. (b) **13¢ was a choice, not a cost leak — two résumés for one job.** The cheapest lever is the product's: *show the cost of A+ before it runs* (Phase 3) and ask why Generate's lift was 0 here. (c) **Output is the largest line (56%)** → Phase 2 (patch output) is where real money is: ~2–2.5¢ of 6.7¢ — the owner's call, design first. (d) **Turn the cache OFF for the interactive path** (`cache: false`) — 0 reads in 11; saves ~0.35¢ a call; turn it back on for D52 bursts. (e) Refusals cost nothing measurable in production — Phase 3's retry cap protects against a cost that has not occurred.

The owner: *one résumé cost **13¢** yesterday; a big share must be analysing the job description — we only need to send the keywords, which our own ATS already has.* **Explore it.** ✅ Owner 10-08: **log it; the A/B is FIVE jobs, run AFTER the changes are built.**

⛔ **THE PREMISE IS PROBABLY SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS — MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING.** From `resume-master/src/generation/`: a generation is **one Sonnet call** (`resume_generate`, thinking off, `max_tokens` 8192) whose **static prompt is ~6,704 tokens** (measured in `promptAssembler.js`'s AL6 table; **input $2 / MTok**, a cache write 1.25×; the interactive path had **0 cache reads**). The job description is **one block** of the user message — roughly **1.5–3.5k tokens ≈ 0.3–0.7¢, i.e. ~2–5% of 13¢.** The big lines are the **output** (the whole résumé HTML, ~3–5k tokens at an output rate several times the input rate — *price not verified*) and the **static prompt written at 1.25× on every call.** ⚠ **A single call comes to ~6–10¢ on this arithmetic, so 13¢ probably means a SECOND call:** a claim-guard **refusal and retry** · **A+** (`resume_enhance`, a second Sonnet call, 8,000 max tokens) · or **`classify`** (Haiku, sends the résumé **and the whole description**) when the domain was not passed in.

⭐ **WHY THE IDEA IS STILL WORTH BUILDING — for reasons other than the description's dollars:** (1) **it removes the fabrication source.** G1's *"Kafka from the JD"* was the model copying a requirement the candidate never claimed; if it never sees the posting it cannot. (2) **it should cut refusals**, and every refusal is a full wasted call — at a 30% refusal rate each *delivered* résumé costs ~43% more. (3) **the precedent exists:** `enhance.js` (A+) already sends the résumé plus a list of selected ATS terms and **no description** — so a **free comparison is already in the ledger**: `resume_enhance` against `resume_generate`.

### PHASE 0 · MEASURE — no build, no spend

1. **A script — `scripts/d70CostBreakdown.mjs` — that assembles the EXACT prompt for a real job and profile WITHOUT calling a model** and prints, per block (static layers 1–3 · profile + claims · **job description** · base résumé), characters → estimated tokens → dollars at the repo's own verified rates. ⚠ Sonnet 5's tokenizer emits **~30% more tokens** than Sonnet 4 for the same text (`enhance.js` says so) — state the factor used. ⛔ **No extra Anthropic call to measure** (D17): estimate from characters, and read real counts from the ledger.
2. **Read the owner's 13¢ résumé in `usage_events`** — every row for that generation: `purpose`, model, input / output tokens, cache write / read. **Report where the 13¢ went:** one call or several · was it A+ · did `classify` run · was there a refused-and-retried generation.
3. **Across ALL `resume_generate` rows:** the **refusal / retry rate**, and the **cache read : write ratio** now that D52 starts generations in bursts.
4. **Does draft always pass `roleFamily` and `domain`?** If not, **`classify` runs and sends the description to a model for nothing** — draft already has D29's tags.
⛔ **Report before building anything below.** If the description turns out to be 3% of the cost, say so; the build then rests on the fabrication and refusal reasons, not the dollars.

### PHASE 1 · KEYWORDS INSTEAD OF THE POSTING — behind a flag

- **Resume Master:** an additive option — `options.jobContext: "description" | "keywords"` — and an optional `job.keywords` object. **Default stays `description`** (the rendered prompt text is pinned byte-for-byte; *"a harmless reformat is a change to every résumé"*) until the A/B passes. Contract: **additive**, and it must be regenerated and re-vendored.
- **What is sent, from draft's own scorer (`scoreAtsLocally`, zero model calls):** the terms the résumé **evidences** (matched), the terms the candidate **claimed**, matched and claimed **verbs**, the **competencies**, and a few **short responsibility phrases extracted deterministically** so the model still knows what the job is (*"payments platform"*, *"on-call"*), plus title, company, seniority and stack.
- ⛔ **What is NEVER sent:** **missing-and-unclaimed terms** (the model could only invent them) and **generic language** (it is not a gap). The posting's text is not sent at all.
- ⛔ **Pre-check, because *"our ATS only gets better"* is an assumption:** measure the extractor's **term recall** on the graded postings — how many of a posting's real requirement phrases reach the keyword list. Terms outside the 6,130-string vocabulary never reach the model; say how many that is.
- **Skip `classify`** by always passing `roleFamily` + `domain` from D29's tags.

### PHASE 2 · WRITE LESS — *conditional on Phase 0*

**If the output turns out to be the largest line, have the model return only what it changes** — the rewritten bullets keyed by id, the skills order, the summary if enabled — and **render the rest deterministically** (the formatter already exists). Expected: **output down 50–70% (~2–4¢)**, and the model **can no longer touch dates, employers or titles.** ⛔ **This changes the output contract and the claim guard** — **write the design first** (`docs/D70_PATCH_OUTPUT.md`) and build only if Phase 0 says output dominates.

### PHASE 3 · THE CHEAP LEVERS

- **Retries:** if a refusal triggers an automatic second generation, **cap it at one and say why in the response**; count them in the ledger by `purpose`.
- **The cache:** pick `cache: true` / `false` **per caller** from the measured read ratio (AL6 made it a lever) — **bursts on, one-shots off.**
- **A+ (`resume_enhance`) is a second call:** state its cost beside a plain Generate and **show it before the user pays for it.**

### PHASE 4 · THE A/B — **FIVE JOBS, AFTER PHASES 1–3 ARE BUILT**

✅ Owner: **5 jobs**, run once the changes exist. ⚠ **Five detects a large cost difference and a catastrophic quality drop; it cannot detect a subtle one** — so choose them to be **different**: a **short** posting, a **long** one, a **non-engineering** domain, one where **the claim guard has refused before**, and one **A+**. **Same base résumé, same claims, same profile for every pair.**
- **Per job, baseline vs new:** **cost** (every call, **retries included**) · **claim-guard pass** · **tailored-vs-base ATS lift** (the deterministic scorer, same weights — ⚠ a lift is only a lift if both numbers come from one scorer) · **a fabrication diff** — any term in the output that is in neither the base résumé nor the candidate's claims · **the owner's BLIND pick** (the two résumés shuffled, unlabelled).
- **Label the calls** (`d70_ab_baseline`, `d70_ab_new`) so they do not pollute the ledger's normal statistics. Total spend is ~$1; **say what it was.**
- ⛔ **Adopt only if:** the new variant is **not worse on ATS lift in at least 4 of 5**, **no fabricated term appears that the baseline avoided**, **refusals are no higher**, and **the owner's blind pick is not clearly the baseline.** Otherwise the flag stays off and the report says why. **A cheaper résumé that is a worse résumé is not a saving.**

⛔ **Not agent work until the owner has seen Phase 0's numbers:** Phase 2's build, and flipping the default. Phases 1 and 3 may proceed once Phase 0 is reported.

## ⛔⭐ D17 · **ONLY RÉSUMÉ GENERATION MAY CALL A MODEL — everything else is in-house or manual.** DECIDED 2026-10-03

⛔ **This is a standing constraint, not a task.** It governs every row above and below it, and it is the
reason the manual export/import paths exist at all.

### The rule

```
MAY CALL A MODEL     résumé generation (and its A+ / cover-letter siblings)

⛔ MAY NOT           everything else. No exceptions without an explicit owner decision
                     recorded here.
```

**Where that bites, by name:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **A76 — the validation corpus** | ⛔ **NOT an API call loop.** Build the **export → grade → import** path: emit the sample as a file the owner grades externally, and import the grades back. ⭐ The machinery already exists — `enrichment_batches`, `enrichment_batch_rows`, the five import guards, the staleness interlock, the revert path. **Reuse it; do not write a second one.** ⛔ The import must **grade blind** the same way the original corpus did — scores withheld from the grader |
| **Enrichment** | Already has the manual path. ⭐ That path is now the **primary** one, not a fallback |
| **PDF→text (A70)** | ⛔ Already decided free and ungated. **O16e's local deterministic extractor is now REQUIRED**, not optional — a model call for a library job is exactly what this rule forbids |
| **ATS scoring** | ⭐ Already zero model calls. **This is the model for everything else** |
| **Capture** | ⭐ Already degrades deterministically via `jobFromLabelledText()`. ⛔ The model path becomes the exception, not the default |
| **Job classification, dedup, slug harvesting, R1 grade-the-posting** | ⛔ Deterministic by construction. None of them may acquire a model call |

### ⭐ Why this is the right call, recorded so it is not re-argued

1. **Cost is bounded and attributable.** One call site, one purpose, one line in `usage_events`.
   Everything else becomes a fixed cost of running the code rather than a per-row charge.
2. ⭐ **Deterministic beats a model at most of these anyway.** Scoring, extraction, dedup and
   classification are **reproducible, testable and free** — and a model made several of them *worse*:
   Groq measured **30.5% Jaccard** on `skills_json`, and `max_tokens: 500` silently truncated
   reasoning models twice.
3. ⭐ **It makes the product survivable.** An unfunded balance currently takes enrichment,
   generation and cover letters to zero. Under this rule it takes **one feature** to zero and the
   rest keeps working — which is what the capture fallback already proved.
4. **The owner can complete the work by hand**, with a free subscription elsewhere, at no cost to
   the project. ⚠ That is only true if **every batch job has an export and an import**.

### ⛔ What every in-house/manual path must have

```
EXPORT     a file the owner can work on outside the product, in a stated format
IMPORT     validated on the way back in. ⛔ The five existing guards are the standard:
           invalid_value · stale · unknown id · concurrency · refusal that reconciles
PROVENANCE a batch row, so a bad import can be identified and reverted whole
REVERT     dry-run first, showing before/after pairs — as the enrichment revert already does
IDEMPOTENT re-importing the same file twice changes nothing
```

⚠ **Measure what it costs to NOT use a model, and say so.** Several of these were justified by a
model being better. ⛔ If the deterministic version is materially worse, **report it rather than
quietly shipping a regression** — the synonym table moved ρ by **+0.000** and that was worth knowing.

### ⚠ The one open question

**Generation itself still calls a model, and it is the most expensive call in the product.** This
rule does not change that — it isolates it. ⭐ **That also makes prompt caching matter more, not
less**, since generation is now the only workload worth optimising.

### Why it is urgent

Pipeline Health shows `adzuna` and `serpapi` as **LIVE SEARCH ONLY · 0 active rows**. ⚠ **Nobody
knows what that status actually means**, and two things depend on the answer:

⭐ **(1) Volume.** The board is ~25 configured companies against ~2,200 that exist. Aggregators see
the **whole market**.
⭐ **(2) ⭐ THE SLUGS.** `COMPANY_LIST_STRATEGY.md` §3C is built on this: **an aggregator result's URL
contains the ATS host AND the company slug.** So every search does not just find a job — **it finds
a company, permanently.** Configure that company once and every future posting arrives same-day,
direct from its board, for free. **That is the engine for ingesting fresh jobs from ATS partner
portals**, and it is the owner's stated reason this matters.

⛔ **If that path is not actually wired, the whole company-growth strategy rests on nothing.**

     · what fraction are the aggregator's own redirect wrapper, an employer's careers page, or a

     COMPANY_LIST_STRATEGY.md §3C needs rewriting. Say so plainly rather than working around it.

4  IS THE HARVEST INFRASTRUCTURE THERE? The owner asks whether "all this discussed infrastructure

## ✅ D1 · JOB CARDS AS BUBBLES — chosen 2026-10-02

**Status 10-03 (21): ✅ BUILT, `c6bd112`, LOCAL** (closes A78, A79) — rows of 2/3/4, grow 1.55 on hover/focus-within, the three-square rail, depth tokens in both themes, Poppins 800 italic self-hosted. Decided: the rail is **always shown on touch**, and on a phone it sits on its own line under the text. ⛔ The ATS square shows the **bar mark, not the number**, until A76 (`ATS_NUMBER_SHOWN` in `shared/atsBands.js`). Shots: `draft-screenshots/d1-bubbles/`.

Replaces the jobs-page card. Sketch: `bubbles2.html`. ⚠ Supersedes the A79 explorations.

### Layout

```
2, 3 or 4 cards PER ROW by viewport width — 3 is the default
flex row · each card flex: 1 1 0 · gap 18px · page padding 28px

HOVER / FOCUS-WITHIN   the card grows to flex-grow 1.55
                       ⛔ THE NEIGHBOURS GIVE UP THE WIDTH. They do NOT reflow to another row,
                         and the row height never changes.
```

⛔ **Sizing is deliberate so compression never truncates.** Card padding `16px 20px`, gaps 18px, and
growth capped at 1.55× — the resting card has enough slack that neighbours compress into
**whitespace**, not into text. Titles ellipsis on one line; nothing wraps or rearranges.
⚠ An earlier sketch used 2.1× growth and 12px gaps and it truncated.

### The card

```
[ logo 52px ] [ company / title / meta ] [ rail — zero width until hover ]

logo        52×52, radius 13, shadow 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.14)
text block  height 52px, vertically centred — shares the logo's exact top and bottom edge
company     ⭐ THE LOGO FACE — heavy italic geometric sans, 17px, letter-spacing -.015em
title       12.5px, --soft
meta        11px, --faint      (all three single-line, ellipsis)
```

⛔ **The company name keeps its hyperlink and loses the underline and the ↗.** ⚠ Keep a non-colour
hover affordance — removing both leaves only colour, which fails for colour-blind users.

⛔ **NO BAND AND NO NUMBER on the card body.** The score lives on the ATS button only.
⚠ **Consequence, and it is deliberate:** nothing on the row shows fit, so **the sort order becomes
the signal** — which is why A75's "ATS match" sort matters more than it looks.

### The rail — three squares, 52px, matching the logo

```
ATS     ⭐ SHOWS THE SCORE when there is one — e.g. 58 with a small "ats" caption,
          green on --okbg.
        ⛔ NO SCORE → the bar icon on --paper, NOT a zero. "Not enough signal" is the scorer
          DECLINING, a correctness state, not a low score.
SAVE    star outline
DRAFT   ⭐ the mark: /d  · --accent fill · shadow tinted orange so it sits in its own colour

⛔ GENERATE and APPLY are REMOVED from the card.
```

**Rail motion:** `max-width: 0 → 196px`, opacity 0 → 1, `margin-left: 0 → 4px`, 0.42s on
`cubic-bezier(.3,.8,.25,1)`. The rail growing is what pushes the neighbours — one motion, not two.

### ⭐ Depth — use it on every control

```
rest   box-shadow: 0 3px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.11), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.66)
hover  0 7px 17px rgba(0,0,0,.15) + translateY(-2px)
press  translateY(0) + 0 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.13)
draft  0 3px 9px rgba(253,70,0,.34)  — tinted, so it reads as orange rather than grey-made-orange
```

The inset top highlight is what makes it feel lit rather than merely dropped.

### ⛔ Before this ships

- **`:focus-within`, not only `:hover`.** Hover-only buttons are unreachable by keyboard.
- ⚠ **Touch has no hover.** Decide: always-visible on touch, or tap-to-reveal. Same shape as the
  swipe/scroll conflict resolved on the deck.
- ⛔ **Self-host the logo typeface.** The sketch loads Poppins from Google Fonts; ⚠ Google Fonts is
  already an open item on the privacy reconciliation and a second third-party request makes it
  worse. A54 established self-hosted fonts with no third-party request — follow it.
  ⚠ Poppins Bold Italic is an **approximation** of the mark; check the source artwork.
- **Tokens only.** The guard fails on any colour outside the token file.
- ⚠ **4-per-row is a wide-monitor column count.** At 1280px the resting cards ellipsis early.

## ✅ D3 · BUG REPORTING AND A TICKET PANEL — queued 2026-10-02, ~~not yet designed~~ **DESIGNED 10-03 (22)**

**Status 10-03 (22): ✅ DESIGNED, nothing built → `docs/BUG_REPORTING.md`; ⏸ the four decisions are O50.** ⛔ **Error handling today is ZERO in draft**: no React error boundary (a render error blanks the app), no `window.onerror`/`unhandledrejection`, no Express error middleware, no `process.on`, no telemetry. Build order: **A** shared payload module (allowlist schema + scrubber + fingerprint) **+ Layer 2 + Layer 1** together, so Layer 2 cannot slip · **B** Layer 3, `/admin/tickets` · **C** "deployed" check, regression reopen, reporter notification · **D** Resume Master's own copy. ⚠ The inspector's redaction covers credentials only (`services/adminSafety.js:17-20`) — reused as an intake refusal; content safety comes from the allowlist in `shared/piiPolicy.js` + server-side scrubbing against what the server knows of the reporter. ⚠ Query strings can carry a session token (`api.js:45`) — never captured. Client SHA compiled into the bundle, not fetched. Production has no `.git` → "deployed" needs the GitHub compare API (a read-only token) or a by-hand check. ⚠ Source maps would publish the source via `express.static` — move them out first.

⛔ **Design the data model and the capture payload first. The panel is the easy half.**

### Why it is worth building now, with zero users

⭐ **The owner IS the first reporter.** Every defect this session — the ATS panel not opening, search
returning nothing, filters doing nothing, "analysing" then erroring — was found by the owner using
the product and relayed through chat. ⚠ **That relay is lossy:** no URL, no job id, no console
error, no build SHA. Half of each investigation has been reconstructing what the owner was looking
at. A report button would have carried all of it for free.

⭐ **And it is the only channel that will exist when strangers arrive.** A user who hits a bug today
has no way to tell anyone.

### How this is normally built — three layers, and most products need all three

```
1  USER-INITIATED        a "Report a problem" control. The user knows something is wrong.
2  AUTOMATIC CAPTURE     an error boundary + a global handler. The product knows before the user
                         says anything — and often before they notice.
3  TRIAGE                somewhere the reports land, get a status, and get closed.
```

⚠ **Most teams build 1 and 3, skip 2, then wonder why the inbox is empty while the product is
broken.** ⭐ **Layer 2 is where the real signal is** — people do not report, they leave.

### ⭐ The context payload is what makes a report useful

A bare "it is broken" costs more to chase than it saves. **Attach automatically, without asking:**

```
WHERE       route, the component, the job / profile / run id in view
WHAT        the console error + stack, the last failed request (method, path, status)
BUILD       ⭐ the commit SHA from /api/version — "which build was this" has been the first
            question in almost every investigation here
WHO         user id, plan, browser, viewport.  ⛔ NOT the résumé. NOT profile contents.
WHEN        timestamp, and the last few user actions if a breadcrumb trail is cheap
```

⛔ **PRIVACY IS THE WHOLE RISK.** A naive reporter scoops up whatever is on screen — which here
means résumé text, addresses, phone numbers, and the **Article 9 columns** (`ethnicity`,
`disability_status`, `veteran_status`). ⛔ **ALLOWLIST the fields captured; never serialise the page
or the store.** The admin inspector already redacts passwords, tokens and session ids — the same
redaction applies here, **by construction, not by remembering**.

⚠ **A screenshot is the highest-value attachment and the highest-risk one.** If offered at all:
opt-in per report, previewed before sending, never automatic.

### The ticket panel

```
STATUS       new → triaged → in progress → fixed → closed   (+ won't fix, duplicate)
SEVERITY     set at TRIAGE, not by the reporter — ⚠ everyone picks "critical"
GROUPING     ⭐ identical stack + route = ONE ticket with a count, not forty.
             The dedup lesson (A49) applies to tickets too.
LINKS        to the job, the run, the user, the build
RESOLUTION   ⭐ the commit that fixed it, AND whether it is DEPLOYED — not merely merged.
             This project has shipped a fix that sat undeployed for a day while being treated
             as done.
```

⭐ **Close the loop with the reporter.** A ticket fixed and never acknowledged teaches people not to
report again — which is the failure mode that makes the whole feature worthless.

### ⚠ Decisions needed before building

1. **Build it, or use a service?** Sentry and similar do layer 2 far better than a first attempt
   will. ⚠ But they are a **third party receiving error payloads from a product that handles
   special-category data** — that is a privacy-reconciliation entry and a policy line. ⭐ A plausible
   split: **in-house for user reports, a service for automatic error capture.** Decide deliberately.
2. **Does the ticket panel live inside the admin panel (A50) or beside it?** A50 is mid-audit; this
   must not collide with it.
3. **Retention.** A report carries personal data, so it needs a stated lifetime and real deletion —
   the same obligation A57 created for stored artifacts.
4. ⚠ **Resume Master needs this too and it is a separate deployment.** One panel reading both, or
   one each? ⛔ The products are *not linked* by decision.

## ✅ D2 · THE ATS REPORT — "THE WEAVE" — chosen 2026-10-02

**Status 10-03 (21): ✅ BUILT, `568b556`, LOCAL**, inside the one report component (all four surfaces). The four open questions answered — **owner, reverse any**: (1) cap **8** threads, the rest folded; (2) plays **once per report per browser session**; (3) the score count-up is built and **dormant until A76** (`ATS_NUMBER_SHOWN`); (4) one component. Also: the drawing starts when the weave is on screen (the deck mounts it mid-slide). Shots: `draft-screenshots/d2-weave/`.

Sketch: `concepts.html` tab 2. Four concepts were built and compared: the scan, the weave, the
stamp, the sieve.

### ⭐ Why the weave won

**A match IS a pairing between two documents, and this draws exactly that.** It was the only one of
the four that is **informative at rest** — when the motion stops, the picture still says something:
asks paired on the left, asks with nothing attached dangling.

⭐ **Dangling asks communicate "missing" better than a red chip does**, because the absence is the
visual rather than a label.

**Why the others lost, recorded so they are not re-proposed:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The scan** | ⭐ Strong second — the only one showing **where** in the résumé you matched, and it makes the product's own line literal. ⚠ Needs a loaded résumé, so it cannot run everywhere |
| **The stamp** | ⭐ Best on brand — cream paper, the tilted mark. ⛔ **Least informative: a satisfying reveal of a list you could have read.** Wears out fastest on repeat opens |
| **The sieve** | ⛔ **Tone problem.** Watching your terms *fail to pass a filter* reads as rejection. The product's voice is *"here is what you could claim"* — the animation argues the opposite of the copy |

### The design

```
TWO COLUMNS          left: what this posting asks     right: what your résumé has
ON OPEN              curves draw between pairs, one at a time, ~260ms apart
                     each pair turns green as its thread lands
AFTER THE PAIRS      unmatched asks switch to a dashed outline — nothing attached
THEN                 the score counts up, ~900ms, eased
```

Thread: `stroke-dasharray` + `stroke-dashoffset` animated to 0, a cubic Bézier with horizontal
control points so it leaves and arrives flat.

### ⛔ Constraints that carry over and must survive

- ⛔ **"Not enough signal" stays visually DISTINCT from "Weak"** — declining is a correctness state.
- ⛔ **Generic language stays separated from genuine gaps**, folded away and labelled **not a gap**.
  Surfacing *Managed* or *collaboration* as a deficiency is a claim that is not true.
- ⛔ **Claim copy unchanged**, and it appears **once**, where the action is — not verbatim three
  times as today: *"claiming a term says it is true of you"*. Nothing is ever pre-selected.
- ⛔ **Depth on every claim control**, per D1.
- ⛔ `prefers-reduced-motion` renders the final state with no drawing.

### ⚠ Open, and they need deciding before build

1. ⛔ **A CAP ON THREADS.** Six is elegant; twenty is spaghetti. Show the top N asks and fold the
   rest — or fall back to the segmented bar above a threshold.
2. **Does it replay on every open?** A panel opened repeatedly will wear out. Once per job, once per
   session, or always — the same question the deck's deal animation had.
3. ⚠ **The score is now the largest element.** That is a stronger claim than a band chip, and
   ⛔ **A76's validation corpus is the condition for it, not a follow-up** — 30 postings graded by
   one person does not support the most prominent element in the product's most-seen free feature.
4. ⭐ **One component, four surfaces** (A52): the deck's left panel, the board, the mobile sheet,
   the public `/tools/ats`. ⛔ Build it once. **Three StampLogo implementations is how the legacy
   brand shipped on every page while the guard passed green.**
